oṃ
śrīmatprabhākaragurutantradhurandhareṇa
mahāmahopādhyāya-śālikanāthamiśreṇa praṇītā prakaraṇapañcikā
nyāyasiddhyākhyayā vyākhyayā viṣamasthalaṭipparāyā
ca samalaṅkṛtā
children.translated_text: Oṃ. The <s>Prakaraṇapañcikā</s> composed by the great <s>Mahāmahopādhyāya</s> <s>Śālikanātha Miśra</s>, who is foremost in bearing the system of the illustrious Guru <s>Prabhākara</s>, adorned with the commentary called <s>Nyāyasiddhi</s> and with glosses on difficult passages.
The first chapter named '<s>Śāstramukham</s>' (Introduction to the Science).
Statement of the subject-matter of the chapter.
We endeavor in the investigation of the meaning of the injunctive sentence regarding <s>svādhyāya</s> (self-study),
Following the view of Guru <s>Prabhākara</s>, for the establishment of the commencement of <s>Mīmāṃsā</s>. // 1 //

children.text:
bhāṭṭamatena mīmāṃsāśāstrānārambhapūrvapakṣaḥ atra kecidācakṣate---
na mīmāṃsāśāstramārambhaṇīyamiti /
taddhi vedavākyārthavicāropāyabhūtanyāyanibandhanam /
na ca vedavākyārtho vicāryo 'sti, yo vicārasya viṣayabhūtaḥ /
nāpyasau vicārya nirṇītaḥ prayojanamavakalpate, apuruṣārthatvāt /
puruṣārthatve hi tasya codanaiva pramāṇaṃ syāt /
na cāvivakṣitārthā sā pramāṇaṃ bhavitumarhati /
nanu śabdānāmautpattikatvādarthaparatvasya nāvivakṣitārthatā yuktā /
satyamevam /
vedenaiva tvanyaparatāmavagamayatāvivakṣitārthatā'padyamānā na śakyā vārayitum /
tathāhi---
svādhyāyo 'dhyetavya ityatra parapreraṇātmakavidhyavaruddhābhāvanā tavyapratyayavācyā pratīyate /
sā ca svabhāvato bhāvyaṃ karaṇamitikartavyatāñcāpekṣate /
tatra1 na tāvadadhyayanameva samānapadopāttaṃ bhāvyatayā sambandhamarhati, apuruṣārthatvāt /
tasmin hi bhāvyatayā svīkriyamāṇe puruṣapravṛttyanupapatteḥ parapreraṇātmakavidhivyāpārabhaṅgaprasaṅgāt /
nāpyekavākyatayā samabhivyāhviyamāṇasya svādhyāyasya bhāvyatayā sambandho 'vakalpate, vidhyānarthakyaprasaṅgāt /
antareṇāpi hi vidhiṃ pratīyata evādhyayanena svādhyāyo 'vāpyata iti /
na ca vrīhīnavahantītivanniyamārtho vidhiriti śakyate vaktum, akratvarthatvādadhyayanasya /
na khalvadhyayanasya hi kratāveva niyamyante, na taṇḍulādisvarūpe /
avadhātenaiva sampāditaistaṇḍulaiḥ kratuphalasiddhiriti pramāṇāntarasyāviṣayatvāttenaiva siddhiriti na kiñcidviruddham /
svādhyāyasvarūpagrahaṇaṃ tvadhyayanenaiva sidhyatīti niyamyamānaṃ mānāntaraviruddham, svayamanadhīyānasyāpi parapuruṣādhīyamānasvādhyāyagrahaṇadarśanāt /
na cādhyayanasvīkṛtenaiva svādhyāyena kratuphalabhāvanāsiddhiriti akratvarthatayā kratusaṃsparśābhāvena niyamānupapatteriti /
etenaivārthāvabodhasyāpi bhāvyatayā sambandho nirasto veditavyaḥ /
tathā hi---
yadyapyadhītātsvādhyāyātphalavatkarmāvabodho dṛśyata iti tasyaiva bhāvyatāvasīyate, tathāpi vināpi vidhinānvayavyatirekābhyāmadhyayanasyārthāvabodhasādhanatvāvamādvidhiranarthaka eva /
na cādhyayanenaivārthāvabodho bhāvayitavya iti niyamavidherarthavattā, prakārāntareṇāpi tatsaṃbhavānniyamānupapatteḥ /
na cādhyayanenaivārthamavabudhyānutiṣṭhatāṃ kratuphalabhāvanāsiddhiriti niyamaḥ saṃbhavati, akratvarthatvādadhyayanasya /
2tasmādviśvajinnyāyena svarge eva bhāvyatayā kalpayitavye prāpte phalamātreyo3 nirddeśādityarthavādikamadhughṛtakulyāditṛptapitrādiprasādalabhyasavrakāmaphapalāvāptireva bhāvyatayāvasīyate /
nanvādyādhyayane na kiñcidārthavādikaṃ phalaṃ śrūyate, tatraiṣāmarthavādānāmaśravaṇāt /
dhāraṇajapayajñavidhyarthavādā hyete /

children.translated_text: Thus say the <s>Vārtikakāra Miśra</s> (i.e., <s>Kumārila</s>):
"In the first study (<s>adhyayana</s>), there is indeed no mention of any fruit;

children.text: dhāraṇe japayajñe ca yā sāpyevaṃ nivāritā" //
children.translated_text: In retention (<s>dhāraṇa</s>), repetition (<s>japa</s>), and sacrifice (<s>yajña</s>), whatever [fruit] there is, is also thus refuted."

The <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prior objection) against the commencement of <s>Mīmāṃsā-śāstra</s> according to the <s>Bhāṭṭa</s> school: Here some say — the <s>Mīmāṃsā-śāstra</s> should not be commenced. For it is a compendium of <s>nyāya</s> (reasoning) that serves as a means for investigating the meaning of Vedic sentences. But there is no meaning of Vedic sentences to be investigated that could serve as the object of such investigation. Nor does the meaning, once investigated and ascertained, serve any purpose, because it is not conducive to human ends (<s>puruṣārtha</s>). For if it were conducive to human ends, injunction (<s>codanā</s>) alone would be the valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>) for it. And an injunction that does not intend to convey a meaning cannot serve as a valid means of knowledge. Now, since words have an inherent (<s>autpattika</s>) connection with their objects, it is not proper to say that they do not intend to convey meaning. True indeed. But the non-intended-meaning-ness that arises when the Veda itself indicates a different purpose (<s>anyaparatā</s>) cannot be prevented. For thus: In '<s>svādhyāyo 'dhyetavyaḥ</s>' (one should study the sacred texts), the <s>bhāvanā</s> (productive force) expressed by the suffix '<s>tavya</s>', which is constrained by the <s>vidhi</s> (injunction) whose nature is prompting another, is understood. And that <s>bhāvanā</s> by its nature requires the <s>bhāvya</s> (what is to be effected), the <s>karaṇa</s> (instrument), and the <s>itikartavyatā</s> (procedure). There, first, <s>adhyayana</s> (study) itself, mentioned in the same word-group, does not deserve connection as the <s>bhāvya</s>, because it is not conducive to human ends. For if study were accepted as the <s>bhāvya</s>, since human activity would become impossible, there would be the unwanted consequence of destroying the operation of <s>vidhi</s> whose nature is prompting another. Nor can the connection of <s>svādhyāya</s>, co-expressed in the same sentence, as the <s>bhāvya</s> be established, because the <s>vidhi</s> would become purposeless. For even without a <s>vidhi</s>, it is understood that <s>svādhyāya</s> is obtained through <s>adhyayana</s>. Nor can it be said that the <s>vidhi</s> serves as a restriction, as in '<s>vrīhīn avahanti</s>' (they thresh rice), because <s>adhyayana</s> is not for the purpose of a <s>kratu</s> (ritual). For <s>adhyayana</s> is not restricted to <s>kratu</s> alone, nor to the form of husked rice and such. Since the fruit of <s>kratu</s> is accomplished with rice-grains produced by threshing alone, and since this falls beyond the scope of another <s>pramāṇa</s>, there is nothing contradictory in its being accomplished by that alone. But the grasping of the form of <s>svādhyāya</s> through <s>adhyayana</s> alone, if restricted thus, contradicts other means of knowledge, since even one who does not study himself is seen to grasp the <s>svādhyāya</s> recited by another person. Nor can the restriction hold that the accomplishment of the <s>bhāvanā</s> for the fruit of <s>kratu</s> is only through <s>svādhyāya</s> obtained by <s>adhyayana</s>, because since <s>adhyayana</s> is not for <s>kratu</s> purposes, there is no contact with <s>kratu</s> and hence restriction is impossible. By this very reasoning, the connection of comprehension of meaning (<s>arthāvabodha</s>) as the <s>bhāvya</s> is also to be understood as refuted. For thus: Even though comprehension of fruitful ritual actions is seen from <s>svādhyāya</s> that has been studied, and thus its status as the <s>bhāvya</s> may be determined, still, even without a <s>vidhi</s>, from positive and negative concomitance (<s>anvaya-vyatireka</s>) of study being a means to comprehension of meaning, the <s>vidhi</s> is indeed purposeless. Nor does a restrictive <s>vidhi</s> that meaning should be comprehended through <s>adhyayana</s> alone have validity, because since that is possible through other means as well, restriction is impossible. Nor can the restriction be that the accomplishment of the <s>bhāvanā</s> for the fruit of <s>kratu</s> is only through those who comprehend meaning through <s>adhyayana</s>, because <s>adhyayana</s> is not for <s>kratu</s> purposes. Therefore, when by the principle of <s>Viśvajit</s> it would follow that <s>svarga</s> (heaven) alone is the <s>bhāvya</s>, since the indication is of mere fruit, what is determined as the <s>bhāvya</s> is only the attainment of desired results obtained through the grace of satisfied ancestors satiated by rivers of honey and ghee as described in <s>arthavāda</s> (laudatory passages). But in the first <s>adhyayana</s> (initial study), no <s>arthavāda</s>-derived fruit is heard, since these <s>arthavādas</s> are not found there. For these are the <s>arthavādas</s> belonging to the injunctions of retention (<s>dhāraṇa</s>), repetition (<s>japa</s>), and sacrifice (<s>yajña</s>).
Thus.

children.text:
satyamevam, tathāpi teṣāmatideśato 'pi labdheryuktaiva tadīyaphalasya bhāvyatā /
tathā hi5 ---
6liṅādiyukteṣu vākyeṣu dve bhāvane 'vagamyete, śabdabhāvanārthabhāvanā ceti /
tatra śabdabhāvanā parapreraṇātmikā /
tasyāḥ puruṣapravṛttirbhāvyam7 /
tayā ca preraṇayā saha yo liṅādīnāṃ vācyavācakabhāvaḥ sambandhaḥ, sa tatra yogyatayā karaṇam /
tadāhurvārtikakāramiśrāḥ---
"liṅādayo hi preraṇāṃ kurvantyabhidadhati ceti" tantravā- 1. 2. 1.ṭa /
pravartyarucyutpādanayogyatayā cārthavādikī stutiritikartavyatā /
tadevamadhyayanavidhau sākṣādaśrutārthavādake śabdabhāvanāyāmitikartavyatābhūtārthavādākāṅkṣiṇyāṃ japayajñādhyayanādatideśenārthavādāḥ svīkriyante /
tadāhurvārtikakāramiśrāḥ---
"anuṣaṅgānumānādyairlabhyante 'nye 'tideśataḥ" iti /
te cātidiṣṭā arthavādā arthabhāvanāyāṃ phalaṃ samarpayanti rātrisatravat /
evamārthavādike phale bhāvyatayāvasite 'dhyayanaṃ samānapadopāttaṃ karaṇākāṅkṣāparipūrakatvena saṃbadhyate /
evañca 8yadaikasmādapūrvaṃ tadetarattadarthamiti nyāyena svādhyāyaśabdavācyo 'kṣararāśirapyadhyayananirvṛttyartha evāvasīyate /
evañcānyaparatvādakṣarāṇāṃ tebhyo 'rthapratipattirevānupapannā, vyutpattivirahāt /
vṛddhavyavahāre hyananyaparāṇyevākṣarāṇyarthāvabodhakatayā vyutpannāni /

children.translated_text: And a word conveys meaning only when dependent on <s>vyutpatti</s> (conventional understanding).

Moreover, whatever comprehension of meaning arises from syllables that serve another purpose — that is to be regarded as mere error, based on a mistaken attribution of non-other-purposiveness due to general perception (<s>sāmānyato-dṛṣṭa</s>).

children.text: apratīyamānaścārtho na vicārasya viṣayaḥ, nāpi prayojanamiti vicārastāvannārabdhavyaḥ, tadanārambhe ca tadapāyabhūtanyāyaparijñānamapyanupayogi /
children.translated_text: And meaning that is not cognized is neither the object of investigation nor its purpose; thus investigation should not be commenced. And in the absence of investigation, the knowledge of <s>nyāya</s> (reasoning) that would remove obstacles to it is also useless.

children.text: tadanupayoge ca tannibandhanaṃ mīmāṃsāśātramanārambhaṇīyamiti pūrvaḥ pakṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: And when that is useless, the <s>Mīmāṃsā-śāstra</s> based on it should not be commenced — this is the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prior position).

True indeed, but even so, since the fruit belonging to those [injunctions] can be obtained through <s>atideśa</s> (extension), the status of their fruit as <s>bhāvya</s> is indeed proper. For thus: In sentences containing <s>liṅ</s> (optative) and other [verbal suffixes], two <s>bhāvanās</s> (productive forces) are understood — <s>śabdabhāvanā</s> (verbal productive force) and <s>arthabhāvanā</s> (objective productive force). There, <s>śabdabhāvanā</s> is of the nature of prompting another. Its <s>bhāvya</s> (what is to be effected) is human activity. And the relation of denotation (<s>vācya-vācaka-bhāva</s>) that <s>liṅ</s> and other suffixes have with that prompting serves as the <s>karaṇa</s> (instrument) by virtue of its fitness. Thus say the <s>Vārtikakāra Miśra</s>: '<s>Liṅ</s> and other [suffixes] indeed both prompt and denote' [<s>Tantravārttika</s> 1.2.1]. And <s>arthavāda</s>-based praise, by its capacity to generate desire that motivates, serves as <s>itikartavyatā</s> (procedure). Thus, in the injunction of <s>adhyayana</s> where no <s>arthavāda</s> is directly heard, when the <s>śabdabhāvanā</s> requires <s>arthavāda</s> as part of its <s>itikartavyatā</s>, <s>arthavādas</s> are borrowed through <s>atideśa</s> (extension) from the <s>japa</s>-<s>yajña</s>-<s>adhyayana</s> injunctions. Thus say the <s>Vārtikakāra Miśra</s>: 'Others are obtained through <s>anuṣaṅga</s> (connection), <s>anumāna</s> (inference), and <s>atideśa</s> (extension).' And those extended <s>arthavādas</s> supply the fruit to the <s>arthabhāvanā</s>, as in the case of the <s>Rātrisatra</s> (night-long sacrifice). Thus, when the <s>arthavāda</s>-derived fruit is established as the <s>bhāvya</s>, <s>adhyayana</s>, mentioned in the same sentence, is connected as fulfilling the expectation for an instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>). And thus, by the principle that 'when from one [sentence] something unprecedented is known, the other is for the purpose of that,' the collection of syllables denoted by the word <s>svādhyāya</s> is also determined to serve the purpose of accomplishing <s>adhyayana</s>. And thus, since the syllables serve another purpose (<s>anyaparatva</s>), the cognition of meaning from them is simply impossible, due to the absence of <s>vyutpatti</s> (conventional understanding). For in the usage of the learned (<s>vṛddha-vyavahāra</s>), only syllables that do not serve another purpose are conventionally understood as conveying meaning.

children.text:
bhāṭṭamatena mīmāṃsārambhasamarthanam---
rāddhāntastu svādhyāyo 'dhyetavya iti svādhyāyasya 9karmatvāvagamātsa eva bhāvyatayāvasīyate /
yadyapi nityatvānnirvarttyakarmatā nāsti svādhyāyasya, vikāryakarmatā vā, adhyayanena tasya vikārānupapatteḥ, tathāpi prāpyatayā tasya karmatā nānupapannā /
ata eva prāpyakarmodāharaṇaṃ vṛttikārasya vedādhyayanam /
yacca karma, tadarthaiva kriyā yuktā /
so 'yaṃ śrauto vinayogaḥ /
na ca svādhyāyasya saktuvaccheṣitvamanupapannam, phalavadarthāvabodhopayogitvāt /
yadyapi cārthāvabodhopayogitvamadhyayanātprāṅnāvagamyate, tathāpi paścādbhāvyapi bhavatyeva prayojanam /
bhāvināpi copayogena śeṣitvaṃ nānupapannam, agnivat /
utpannānāṃ hyagnīnāṃ viniyogāvagamaḥ, nāvagataviniyogānāmutpattiḥ /
āhavanīyādiśabdānāmalaukikārthatayā prāgvyutpattyavagamādarthānavagateḥ homādiṣu viniyogāsaṃbhavāt /
tathā coktam---
"bhūtabhāvyupayogaṃ hi dravyaṃ saṃskāramarhati /
" [tantrāvā- 2. 1. 4.] nanu cārthāvabodhopayogitayā saṃskāravidhiranarthaka evetyuktam iti /
nānarthakaḥ, niyamārthatayārthavattvāt /
nanu ca niyamo na sambhavati, apratusaṃsparśitvāditktam /
tanna sambhavati svābhāvikārthaparatvānusāreṇa kratvanupraveśe kratusaṃsparśitāyā evocitatvāt /
yadi khalvadhyayanavidheḥ kratvanupraveśitā nāśrīyate, tadā śabdānāṃ vṛddhavyavahāravyutpannānāṃ svābhāvikārthaparatā hīyeta /
jahatsvārthatvaṃ ca na nyāyyamiti kratuphalabhāvanānupraveśyevādhyayanasaṃskāro yuktaḥ /
tatra karmavidhiṣvevaṃ niyamavarṇanā adhyayanāvirbhāvitaireva karmavidhibhirarthamavabudhyānutiṣṭhatāṃ kratuphalabhāvanāsiddhiriti /
arthavādeṣu tvadhyayanāvirbhāvitārthavādaprarocitāḥ kriyamāṇāḥ kratavaḥ phalabhāvanāya alamiti /
mantreṣu punaradhyayanaparigṛhītaireva mantraiḥ kratuṣu padārthasmaraṇaṃ phalabhāvanāṅgamiti /
children.translated_text: And regarding <s>mantras</s>, the recollection of word-meanings in rituals through <s>mantras</s> grasped through <s>adhyayana</s> alone is an auxiliary to the <s>bhāvanā</s> of fruit.
And the restriction of time and the restriction of observances (<s>vrata</s>) and such are dependent on the restriction of <s>adhyayana</s>.
"Having performed the <s>upākarma</s> (initiation ceremony) on the full moon of <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> or <s>Prauṣṭhapada</s>, according to the prescribed rules,
The devoted <s>brāhmaṇa</s> should study the <s>Chandas</s> (Vedas) for four and a half months."

The established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>) supporting the commencement of <s>Mīmāṃsā</s> according to the <s>Bhāṭṭa</s> school: The correct view is that since from '<s>svādhyāyo 'dhyetavyaḥ</s>' (one should study the sacred texts) the objecthood (<s>karmatva</s>) of <s>svādhyāya</s> is understood, <s>svādhyāya</s> itself is established as the <s>bhāvya</s> (what is to be effected). Although, due to its eternality, <s>svādhyāya</s> cannot have the status of an object being produced (<s>nirvartya-karmatā</s>), nor the status of an object being modified (<s>vikārya-karmatā</s>) since modification of it through <s>adhyayana</s> is impossible, nevertheless its objecthood as something to be reached (<s>prāpya-karmatā</s>) is not impossible. Hence the <s>Vṛttikāra</s>'s (<s>Śabara</s>'s) example of an object-to-be-reached is Vedic study (<s>vedādhyayana</s>). And activity is proper only for the purpose of that which is the object. This is a Vedic injunction (<s>śrauta-viniyoga</s>). Nor is the subordination (<s>śeṣitva</s>) of <s>svādhyāya</s>, like barley-meal (<s>saktu</s>), impossible, because it is useful for comprehending meaning that leads to [ritual] fruits. And even though the usefulness for comprehension of meaning is not known before <s>adhyayana</s>, still, even something occurring later can serve as a purpose. And subordination through even a future use is not impossible, as in the case of fire (<s>agni</s>). For it is the ascertainment of the application of fires already produced, not the production of fires whose application is already known. Since before <s>vyutpatti</s> (conventional understanding) is grasped, meaning is not understood from words like <s>Āhavanīya</s> which have non-ordinary meanings, their application in <s>homa</s> (oblation) and other rites is not possible. And thus it has been said: 'For a substance that has present or future utility deserves consecration (<s>saṃskāra</s>)' [<s>Tantravārttika</s> 2.1.4]. Now, [the objection is that] since <s>svādhyāya</s> is useful for comprehension of meaning, the injunction of consecration is indeed purposeless, as stated. [Reply:] It is not purposeless, because it has meaning as a restrictive injunction. But [the objection is that] restriction is not possible since <s>adhyayana</s> has no connection with <s>kratu</s>, as stated. That is not valid, because when entry into <s>kratu</s> is followed in accordance with the natural meaning-directedness of words, contact with <s>kratu</s> is indeed proper. For if the entry of the <s>adhyayana</s>-injunction into <s>kratu</s> is not accepted, then the natural meaning-directedness of words, conventionally understood through the usage of the learned, would be compromised. And since abandoning one's own meaning (<s>jahat-svārthatva</s>) is improper, the consecration through <s>adhyayana</s> is proper only when entering into the <s>bhāvanā</s> of <s>kratu</s>-fruit. There, regarding <s>karmavidhis</s> (injunctions of ritual acts), the restriction is as follows: the accomplishment of the <s>bhāvanā</s> of <s>kratu</s>-fruit is through those who comprehend meaning through the very <s>karmavidhis</s> manifested by <s>adhyayana</s> and then perform accordingly. But regarding <s>arthavādas</s> (laudatory passages), the rituals performed as inspired by <s>arthavādas</s> manifested through <s>adhyayana</s> are sufficient for the <s>bhāvanā</s> of fruit.
<s>Manusmṛti</s> Chapter 2, verse 2.49.11
"The initiated twice-born of the highest class (<s>dvijottama</s>) should seek alms saying '<s>bhavat</s>' at the beginning;
The <s>kṣatriya</s> (royal class) should place '<s>bhavat</s>' in the middle, and the <s>vaiśya</s> (merchant class) should place '<s>bhavat</s>' at the end."

children.translated_text: . Thus, since the syllables do not serve another purpose, and since the cognition of fruitful ritual actions arises, the object and purpose of investigation are obtained, and thus the <s>śāstra</s> should be commenced. And since, upon obtaining the object and purpose, the investigation naturally follows after <s>adhyayana</s>, the stay in the <s>guru</s>'s house (<s>gurukulasthiti</s>) has purpose. Remembering the cessation of <s>gurukulavāsa</s> that comes after <s>adhyayana</s>, the <s>smṛti</s> statement '<s>vedamadhītya snāyāt</s>' (having studied the Veda, one should perform the graduation bath) also indicates its basis in <s>nyāya</s> (reasoning). Considering that <s>svādhyāya</s>, being directed toward meaning, has intended meaning (<s>vivakṣitārthatā</s>), the <s>sūtrakāra</s> (author of the sūtras) states the object and purpose of investigation: '<s>athāto dharmajijñāsā</s>' (<s>Pūrva-Mīmāṃsā Sūtra</s> 1.1.1) — 'Now, therefore, the inquiry into <s>dharma</s>.'
And this has been explained in the verse:
"This first <s>sūtra</s>, '<s>athāto dharmajijñāsā</s>,' was composed
To state the object called <s>dharma</s> and the purpose of <s>Mīmāṃsā</s>."

children.translated_text: Because performance is accomplished from another source.
From what other source? From the prompting by the injunction of making a teacher (<s>ācāryakaraṇa-vidhi</s>).

children.translated_text: What then is the injunction of making a teacher? "The twice-born (<s>dvija</s>) who, having initiated a pupil, teaches him the Veda,
Together with the ritual formulae (<s>kalpa</s>) and the secret teachings (<s>rahasya</s>) — him they call the teacher (<s>ācārya</s>)."

[<s>Mīmāṃsā-Ślokavārttika</s> 1.1.11] Even though stated at length, that is improper. For in sentences containing <s>liṅ</s> (optative) and other suffixes, <s>bhāvanā</s> does not require another <s>bhāvya</s> (object to be effected), because <s>apūrva</s> (the unprecedented result), which is the <s>bhāvya</s>, is already denoted by its own word. For <s>liṅ</s> and other suffixes denote a <s>bhāvanā</s> in which <s>apūrva</s>, as the principal element belonging to the <s>bhāvya</s> category, has become subordinate — this has been more carefully demonstrated in the <s>Viṣayakaraṇīya</s> section. Therefore, in the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s>, there is no connection with <s>arthavāda</s>-derived fruit when the <s>bhāvya</s> is being sought. Nor in the <s>siddhānta</s> is there a connection of <s>svādhyāya</s> as something to be accomplished. How then is the postulation of fruits like <s>svarga</s> (heaven) in the <s>Viśvajit</s> and other sacrifices? Listen to how that is: The <s>apūrva</s>, understood as what is to be produced (<s>kārya</s>), depends for its own realization on the performance of <s>yāga</s> (sacrifice) and other acts that serve as its connected instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>). And without an agent (<s>kartṛ</s>), that performance is impossible. And without qualification (<s>adhikāra</s>), the status of agent is not obtained. And without a person to be enjoined (<s>niyojya</s>), qualification is not established. And since an unqualified person cannot serve as the <s>niyojya</s>, the desire for heaven (<s>svargakāmanā</s>) is postulated as the qualifying attribute. And if the desire for heaven qualifies the <s>niyojya</s>, then, as in <s>Agnihotra</s> and other rites, <s>svarga</s> too is accomplished through the injunction (<s>niyoga</s>). Let it be so; but then here too, let the <s>arthavāda</s>-derived fruit be connected as the qualifying attribute of the <s>niyojya</s>, as in the <s>Rātrisatra</s> (night-long sacrifice). No —

children.translated_text: — this is inferred from <s>smṛti</s> (remembered tradition): one should achieve the status of <s>ācārya</s> by initiating a pupil and teaching him the Veda — such is its form. And since the status of <s>ācārya</s> is non-mundane (<s>alaukika</s>), like the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire and others, the prescription of the means for its production is indeed proper. There, the qualification belongs by implication to one who desires to become an <s>ācārya</s>, like the restriction on earning wealth. There, since the giving of <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (fees) and the conduct prescribed for the pupil are seen, the desire to become an <s>ācārya</s> is itself the desire for those gains. Just as the status of being initiated (<s>dīkṣitatva</s>) is accomplished by the <s>Dīkṣaṇīyā</s> (consecration rite), so the status of <s>ācārya</s> is accomplished by teaching the Veda. And <s>upanayana</s> (initiation), understood through the <s>ktvā</s>-suffix as having the same agent as teaching, since without sharing the same agent the single-performance (<s>ekaprayoga</s>) relationship would be impossible, and since without the relation of principal and subsidiary single-performance is impossible, stands as a subsidiary to teaching, which serves as the instrument (<s>karaṇa</s>) of the <s>bhāvanā</s> of <s>ācāryaka</s> (teacher-status). And dependent on that is the restriction 'one should initiate a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> at eight years' and similar rules. Since <s>upanayana</s> does not by its nature serve the purpose of bringing the initiate near, it is a subsidiary of that [teaching] only through that means. And since the proximity of the initiate is not useful apart from teaching but is useful for teaching, when the need for the initiate as object arises, having begun with <s>upanayana</s>, the study enjoined in '<s>svādhyāyo 'dhyetavyaḥ</s>' is understood as the act directed toward the initiate. And study is useful for teaching. This is correct. Therefore, the injunction of teaching, employing <s>upanayana</s> as its own subsidiary, also employs study, since it is impossible without it. And since the injunction of <s>svādhyāya</s>-study, having achieved its purpose through the study prompted by that teaching injunction, does not require another qualification, this is not a case for the <s>Viśvajit</s> principle, nor for the <s>Rātrisatra</s> principle, because those two apply only to injunctions whose scope is not prompted by something else. For this very reason, those two principles do not enter into the injunctions of <s>prayāja</s> (preliminary oblations) and the like. Otherwise, even in the <s>siddhānta</s>, since study would be prompted by the mention of desire for fruits, even <s>śūdras</s> and others would have qualification for ritual acts accomplished through knowledge. Therefore, since <s>adhyayana</s> is prompted by the injunction of teaching, only those for whom <s>upanayana</s> is prescribed obtain the <s>mantras</s> prompted by it, and hence <s>śūdras</s> and others lack qualification. And thus, when study is prompted by another injunction, the objection of the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> based on the <s>Rātrisatra</s> principle is not appropriate. Nor is it proper to say that the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> holds when not prompted by that, and the <s>siddhānta</s> when prompted — because there is no reason for its not being prompted. And what was said about the <s>vidhi</s> being for restriction — that is improper, because the sentence has meaning through the prescription of <s>svādhyāya</s>-study for the purpose of accomplishing the injunction (<s>niyoga</s>). In '<s>svādhyāyo 'dhyetavyaḥ</s>', the <s>vidhi</s> is expressed by the suffix '<s>tavya</s>'. And this cannot be taken as a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>) of an injunction related to <s>kratu</s> (ritual), as in the '<s>avahanti</s>' cases, due to the absence of proximity of <s>kratu</s>-injunctions. For it is only through proximity that <s>kratu</s>-injunctions are recognized, and hence the acceptance of restatement of <s>kratu</s>-injunctions is made there. But here there is no such proximity. Nor is there recognition of <s>kratu</s>-injunctions through the connection of word-meanings, as in '<s>parṇamayī jujūrbhavatī</s>' (the leaf-made ladle grows old), because <s>svādhyāya</s> has a variable connection with <s>kratu</s>, since meaningless syllables like '<s>hum</s>' and such are seen to be included within <s>svādhyāya</s>. Since the injunction (<s>niyoga</s>) is understood here as something to be accomplished, for this very reason the connection of <s>svādhyāya</s> as the desired object (<s>īpsita-karma</s>) is established, because having two things to be accomplished in one sentence would be contradictory. And the absence of contradiction through <s>svādhyāya</s> connecting as a qualifying attribute of the <s>niyojya</s>, like <s>svarga</s>, is not possible, because the grasping of <s>svādhyāya</s> is not a fruit of injunction. For only what is a fruit arising from injunction qualifies the <s>niyojya</s> as something to be accomplished, and nothing else — this has been shown in the third <s>adhyāya</s>: in the passage 'You do not confuse the objects and persons to be enjoined.' Therefore, since the sentence has meaning merely through establishing that the injunction has study as its object, the <s>vidhi</s> does not serve as a restriction through postulating entry into <s>kratu</s>. The view of the old <s>Prabhākara</s> school (<s>jarat-Prabhākara-mata</s>) and its refutation: Others, however, raise the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> thus: Study (<s>adhyayana</s>), being prompted by the injunction of teaching (<s>adhyāpana-vidhi</s>), is a subsidiary (<s>aṅga</s>) of teaching, and since <s>svādhyāya</s> serves another purpose for the sake of accomplishing that, it has unintended meaning (<s>avivakṣitārthatā</s>). That is improper, because mere prompting does not establish a purposive relation (<s>tādarthya</s>). One might think: just as in the <s>Prajāpativrata</s> observances, since an independent agent is understood, the <s>niyojya</s> is postulated for the sake of establishing the qualification that causes it, so too from observing prompting, a purposive relation is established. That is not so, because prompting does not invariably imply purposive relation. For even without a purposive relation, <s>adhyayana</s> is prompted by <s>karmavidhis</s> (ritual injunctions) merely through its helpfulness. How then is the subsidiary status (<s>aṅgatva</s>) of the oneness (<s>ekatva</s>) of the sacrificial animal (<s>paśu</s>) and such established? First, the case-ending (<s>vibhakti</s>) does not by itself denote oneness as related to <s>kratu</s>, so that there could be application through the sentence, like redness (<s>aruṇya</s>) and such. For case-endings denote by verbal expression only the meaning inherent in the stem-meaning (<s>prātipadikārtha</s>). Nor is the oneness predicated of the instrument, nor is instrumentality predicated of what has number, since instrumentality and oneness are denoted simultaneously. Therefore, the subordination of the number denoted by the case-ending is not through injunction. Yet subordination is accepted, and that is established through prompting alone. Not so — even there, the subordination is not through proximate mention (<s>aupādānika</s>) but rather through indication (<s>laiṅgika</s>). The capacity of the thing itself is what is called 'indication' (<s>liṅga</s>). And number by its very nature delimits what is to be numbered, and is thus for the sake of the thing numbered. But the connection with the sacrificial animal and such, which belongs to the context (<s>grāhaka</s>), is proximate — because mere connection with the stem-meaning that is the thing numbered would result in contradiction with the contextual connection. For by mere proximity and co-recitation, even the meaning of the case-ending is denoted only as connected for the purpose of the context; and since that is otherwise inexplicable, surpassing the intrinsic connection based on mere denotation, there is the inference of connection with the thing numbered that serves as the instrument — hence even there the subordination is not through proximate mention. Then let the application of <s>adhyayana</s> in teaching be established through indication alone. That cannot be so, because indicative application depends on a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of knowledge) that establishes a general connection. And there is no <s>pramāṇa</s> establishing a general connection for this. But does not the causative suffix (<s>ṇic</s>) establish the subordination of study, which is the root-meaning? Not so, because since the activity of the causer (<s>prayojaka</s>) is the cause of the arising of the activity of the caused (<s>prayojya</s>), the reverse subordination would follow.

The principles of sentence (<s>vākya</s>), context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>), position (<s>sthāna</s>), and designation (<s>samākhyā</s>) should not even be suspected as applying <s>adhyayana</s> to <s>adhyāpana</s> (teaching) as instruments of application.
Moreover, there is a contradiction with the commentary text (<s>ṭīkā-grantha</s>) for those who maintain subsidiary status (<s>aṅgatva</s>).
For thus says the venerable master:
"Because of being caused (<s>prayojyatva</s>) and because of not being a subsidiary (<s>anaṅgatva</s>), there arises doubt."

children.translated_text: And since study has usefulness for the student through its utility for comprehension of meaning, he is the eligible person for it.
And this eligibility is not known before study, but is known in the period after study.

But the study of <s>svādhyāya</s> is accomplished thus: "Having performed the <s>upākarma</s> (initiation ceremony) on the full moon of <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> or <s>Prauṣṭhapada</s>, according to the prescribed rules,
the devoted <s>brāhmaṇa</s> should study the <s>Chandas</s> (Vedas) for four and a half months."

Therefore, the objection should be raised through the very fact of non-subsidiarity (<s>anaṅgatā</s>). But how can the objection be raised through non-subsidiarity? It is replied: For every injunction (<s>vidhi</s>) terminates in an eligible person (<s>adhikārin</s>). And that no one has eligibility (<s>adhikāra</s>) in the injunction of study has already been stated, due to the absence of direct hearing, and because postulation is impossible through being motivated by the injunction of teaching. There, that very eligibility which is in the prompting injunction — it is proper that this alone is the purpose, due to its being the first to present itself (<s>prathamopanipātitvāt</s>). And moreover, that which is non-subsidiary to something is also its purpose, just as oblations (<s>homa</s>) and such are the purpose of the consecration of fires (<s>ādhāna</s>). [Objection:] But since the eligibility of the student himself in study is understood through study's having as its fruit the comprehension of ritual actions that follow immediately thereafter, the status of this alone as the purpose of the <s>svādhyāya</s> injunction is proper, due to its being more intrinsic (<s>antaraṅgatva</s>). [Reply:] No, because it arises only subsequently. For when the availability is equal, the more intrinsic is stronger. But the availability of these two types of eligibility is not equal — due to the prior presentation of the eligibility in the prompting injunction, and due to the subsequent arising of the eligibility based on comprehension of meaning. And when what is indicated by the injunction of study is that the establishment of eligibility in the injunction of teaching is the purpose of study, then since <s>svādhyāya</s> serves the purpose of accomplishing study, it has other-directedness (<s>anyaparatva</s>), and hence non-intended-meaning-ness (<s>avivakṣitārthatva</s>). And meaning that is not intended is not to be investigated; thus, thinking that by mere Veda-study itself the purpose of staying at the <s>guru</s>'s house is fulfilled, and therefore departure from the <s>guru</s>'s house after study is proper, the <s>smṛti</s> says: '<s>vedamadhītya snāyāt</s>' — 'Having studied the Veda, one should bathe (graduate)' [<s>Baudhāyana Gṛhyasūtra</s> 6.1]. And here, bathing is not enjoined as having an unseen purpose; rather, the restriction of non-bathing stated as '<s>brahmacārī na snāyāt</s>' (a <s>brahmacārin</s> should not bathe) — its termination, which naturally follows upon the cessation of the restrictions that are subsidiary to study, is what is stated. And since the cessation of residence at the <s>guru</s>'s house and such naturally follows, being on par with the restriction of non-bathing, the cessation of all <s>brahmacārin</s>-duties after study is stated. And thus, since investigation is not drawn in by the injunction of study, the <s>Mīmāṃsā-śāstra</s> based on <s>nyāya</s> (reasoning) that serves as the means [of investigation] need not be commenced — this is the prior position (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>). The established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>) according to [<s>Prabhākara</s>'s] own view: But the correct conclusion is — although the eligibility in the prompting injunction arises first, still it is not proper that its accomplishment is the purpose. Rather, the eligibility of the student himself, though arising after study, by virtue of having as its fruit the visible comprehension of meaning, is proper to accept as the purpose, because it inheres in the agent (<s>kartṛsamavāyitvāt</s>). For it is proper that the agent who performs an action has sovereignty over it, due to being more intrinsic. And there is no reason to postulate the termination of eligibility merely from seeing the injunction, since performance is accomplished by the prompting of another alone. Where indeed performance cannot be obtained without postulating the termination of eligibility, there eligibility that was not known prior to performance is to be established through entering into it. But here, since performance is obtained through the prompting of the teaching injunction alone without postulating the termination of eligibility, priority is of no consequence. Due to being more intrinsic, the eligibility of the student alone is proper. Thus, since the performance of the study-injunction is accomplished by the prompting of another alone, there is no person enjoined (<s>niyojya</s>). But there is indeed an eligible person (<s>adhikārin</s>). For whoever performs an action is the eligible person for it.

children.translated_text: Because otherwise study would be impossible.
Because study is prohibited for the uninitiated (<s>anupanīta</s>).
"One should not utter the <s>Brahman</s> (Veda) except for the offering of <s>svadhā</s> (oblation to ancestors);
He is equal to a <s>śūdra</s> until he is born from the Veda."

[<s>Manusmṛti</s> 4.98] Thus, when study is carried out in this manner, comprehension of meaning arises from the Vedic sentences for one who has been refined by the study of the auxiliary sciences (<s>aṅga</s>). And this student thinks: 'Study is for my sake, since it produces comprehension of ritual actions useful to me.' That eligibility which lies between Veda-study and hearing of <s>Mīmāṃsā</s> — this is the fundamental purpose of the <s>śāstra</s>. Having considered this very eligibility, fathers and others, having attracted some by gifts of wealth and such, initiate sons and others for Vedic study. And some awakened ones initiate themselves.

children.translated_text: If one were to depart from the <s>guru</s>'s house without having determined the meaning of the Veda, then having taken a wife, being unable to perform the duties — the obligatory (<s>nitya</s>) and occasional (<s>naimittika</s>) rites such as the <s>Śrauta Agnihotra</s> etc. — that fall upon him, he would be ruined.

children.text: tasmādadhyayanasyānantarameva vedārtho vicārayitavya iti vicāropāyabhūtanyāyanibandhanaṃ mīmāṃsāśāstramārabdhavyamiti siddham /
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is established that the meaning of the Veda should be investigated immediately after study, and thus the <s>Mīmāṃsā-śāstra</s>, based on <s>nyāya</s> (reasoning) that serves as the means of investigation, should be commenced.
The chapter called '<s>Śāstramukha</s>' (Introduction to the Science), to reveal even the profound import of the Guru [<s>Prabhākara</s>] —
was composed by <s>Śālikanātha</s>; this chapter is most lucid. [2]

[<s>Manusmṛti</s> 2.172] Thus, the description of the established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>) has been made based on the teaching-injunction inferred from <s>smṛti</s>. The established conclusion according to the <s>Vivaraṇa</s>: But others, following the teaching-injunction directly heard in the Veda, say thus: If the purpose of the <s>svādhyāya</s>-study injunction were the eligibility in the teaching-injunction, then since the teaching-injunction too falls within <s>svādhyāya</s>, by virtue of its non-intended-meaning-ness, even being prompted by it would be impossible. For one's own branch (<s>śākhā</s>) is denoted by the word <s>svādhyāya</s>. And since the directly studied teaching-injunction would certainly fall within the branch of some branch-followers, due to the non-intended-meaning-ness of <s>svādhyāya</s>, its non-intended-meaning-ness too follows, so its prompting capacity cannot be maintained. Therefore, the eligibility of the student, by virtue of its utility for comprehension of meaning that arises subsequently, is the purpose of the study-injunction. [Objection:] But since from the understanding of the established injunction '<s>svādhyāyo 'dhyetavyaḥ</s>' (one should study the sacred texts), study serves the purpose of accomplishing that injunction; due to its other-directedness, the intention to convey meaning is indeed hard to maintain. [Reply:] Not so. If study were only for the purpose of accomplishing the injunction, this would indeed be so. But when comprehension of meaning is also accepted as a purpose, then meaning-directedness too exists, so there is no non-intended-meaning-ness. [Question:] But how can there be two purposes in a single sentence? It is replied: The accomplishment of the injunction itself is the verbal (<s>śābda</s>) purpose, while the comprehension of meaning is the objective (<s>ārtha</s>) purpose — so there is no contradiction. And since that purpose called comprehension of meaning is not accomplishable by study alone, the study-injunction itself draws in investigation for the accomplishment of its own purpose. And since investigation is based on <s>nyāya</s> (reasoning), and since <s>nyāya</s>s are knowable through <s>Mīmāṃsā</s>-knowledge, and since <s>Mīmāṃsā</s>-knowledge depends on a teacher, the venerable <s>sūtrakāra</s>, thinking that one should not depart from the <s>guru</s>'s house after Veda-study, to show that the <s>smṛti</s> is the root of the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> position, prohibiting departure from the <s>guru</s>'s house that would follow study through the instruction of <s>dharma</s>-inquiry, states this: '<s>athāto dharmajijñāsā</s>' — 'Now, therefore, the inquiry into <s>dharma</s>.' And only the departure from the <s>guru</s>'s house that contradicts the investigation of Vedic sentence-meaning is prohibited, not the cessation of all other duties such as begging (<s>bhikṣā</s>), wandering, celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>), etc. And one who has not completed all <s>brahmacārin</s>-restrictions is not a graduate (<s>snātaka</s>), so he is not eligible for taking a wife, because the <s>smṛti</s> remembers wife-taking only for the <s>snātaka</s>: '<s>snātakaḥ sadṛśīṃ bhāryāṃ vinded</s>' — 'The graduate should find a suitable wife' [<s>Gautama Dharmasūtra</s> 4.1]. Therefore, staying at the <s>guru</s>'s house and setting aside all other <s>brahmacārin</s>-duties, the meaning of the Veda should be investigated, because what is not investigated remains undetermined.
Thus, in the <s>Prakaraṇapañcikā</s> composed by the great <s>Mahāmahopādhyāya Śrī Śālikanātha Miśra</s>,
the first chapter named '<s>Śāstramukha</s>' (Introduction to the Science)
is concluded.
The second chapter named '<s>Nītipatha</s>' (The Path of Reasoning).
Statement of the subject-matter of the chapter.
Just as the suspicion of non-contact of words with their objects (<s>arthāsaṃsparśitā</s>) is refuted,
so do the disciples of Guru <s>Prabhākara</s> make their effort. [1]
The prior objection (<s>pūrvapakṣa</s>):
Here, from the perception that ordinary sentences can deviate [from truth],
some disputants assert the non-contact of words with their objects. [2]
Ascertainment is the contact with the object, and that belongs only to what does not deviate from the object;
it belongs only to perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) and such, while verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>) is subject to deviation. [3]
For even without an [actual] object, cognition arises from words,
such as 'There is a herd of elephants on the tip of a finger' and similar [false statements]. [4]
Nor can it be said here, as in the case of the cognition of silver in a shell (<s>śukti</s>),
that this is an error due to non-apprehension, because there is no distinction in the cause. [5]
For defective causes are incapable of producing a complete effect;
therefore, non-apprehension of the distinction is proper in [cases like] shell-silver etc. [6]

children.text: iha tu jñānaheturyaḥ śabdaḥ sa na viśiṣyate /
children.translated_text: But here, the word (<s>śabda</s>) that is the cause of cognition is not differentiated [whether the speaker is truthful or not];

children.text: viśiṣyate yastu vaktā sa jñānasya na kāraṇam // 7 //
children.translated_text: while the speaker, who is differentiated, is not the cause of cognition. [7]
If the speaker too were a cause of cognition, like sense-organs and such,
then through his defect there would be non-apprehension. [8]
But the speaker is useful merely for the manifestation of words;
cognition is produced by words alone, independent [of the speaker]. [9]
And no defect whatsoever is found in them [i.e., in words];
defect is the cause of non-apprehension, and in its absence, apprehension is clear. [10]
Therefore, this cognition produced by words is indeed such
that it transcends the object — so how can there be ascertainment of the object through it? [11]

children.text: yenāpi hi vinā yasya sadbhāva31 upapadyate /
children.translated_text: For that whose existence is established even without something —
ascertainment by that [thing] is not proper — this is a well-spoken saying. [12]
[Objection:] But if so, how could there be practical activity (<s>vyavahṛti</s>) from the statements of trustworthy persons (<s>āpta</s>)?

children.text: vyavahāro hi lokasya kathaṃ syānniścayaṃ vinā? // 13 //
children.translated_text: For how could the practical dealings of the world proceed without certainty? [13]
It is replied: Worldly practical activity is seen to proceed mostly

children.text: prāyaśo dṛśyate tena ca kiñcidiha duṣyati // 14 //
children.translated_text: even from doubt, and therefore nothing is harmed here. [14]
Moreover, by considering the trustworthiness (<s>āptatva</s>) of the speaker, ascertainment of the object in that case
is somehow established even through another means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>). [15]
But the Veda, since its objects are supra-mundane (<s>alaukika</s>), and since there is indeed no speaker,

children.text: aho bata daśāṃ kaṣṭāmupanīto hi paṇḍitaiḥ // 16 //
children.translated_text: alas, has been brought to a dire state by the learned! [16]
The established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>):
Here, those of keen intellect strive to counter [the objection];
the deviation of cognition [produced by words] is refuted on the path of reasoning (<s>nayavīthī</s>). [17]
Listen with attention to the nature of human words as well;
the learned do not accept their separate existence from inference (<s>anumāna</s>). [18]
For ordinary speech, whose composition depends on a person,
being suspected of falsity, does not by itself ascertain the object. [19]
For human beings are seen composing words
whose meanings are not mutually connected; therefore there is no certainty of syntactic connection (<s>anvaya</s>). [20]
Some [speak falsely] through error, some through defect of intention,
some through carelessness, and some through incapacity — [thus] some are speakers of unconnected [statements]. [21]
Even though the word-meanings stated by them have fitness for syntactic connection,
Nevertheless, even from the perception of what is not connected, there is no certainty of connection. // 22 //
There, by the word 'certainty' (<s>niścaya</s>), cognition alone is meant;
In the absence of certainty of connection, therefore, there is cognition alone, not connection. // 23 //
Since the unreliability of its composition is suspected, a human statement,
When merely heard, does not produce certainty regarding the object. // 24 //
So long as the speaker's prior [cognition], unknown [to the hearer], another means of knowledge,
Having intended meaning as its object, grounded in sense-organ-based meaning, // 25 //

children.text: tasya jñānaṃ ca vākyena liṅgabhūtena gamyate /
children.translated_text: And his knowledge is ascertained through the sentence, which serves as an inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>),
'He speaks only having known the meaning' — when this has been determined, // 26 //
His knowledge being invariably connected with the sentence, the sentence indicates his knowledge;
And knowledge being inseparable from the object, through that there is certainty about the object too. // 27 //
When the object is thus ascertained, thereafter that object is known through the sentence;
In that condition, the sentence would have the status of a restatement (<s>anuvāda</s>). // 28 //
But previously, that [sentence] serves as an inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) for ascertaining the speaker's knowledge;
For the sentence, being produced from the speaker's knowledge, is accepted as its effect. // 29 //
And the establishment of the cause from the effect is through inference for all;
Therefore a human statement (<s>pauruṣeya vākya</s>) is not called <s>śāstra</s> (authoritative scripture). // 30 //
And this being so, this deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) of the inferential mark is observed;
Not of <s>śāstra</s> — so how would it lack contact with the object? // 31 //

children.text: liṅgasyāpi na caivāyaṃ vyabhicāro 'sti kintu yaḥ /
children.translated_text: And this deviation does not actually exist even of the inferential mark; rather, one who
Cannot distinguish between a mark and a non-mark is a dull-witted person. // 32 //
His usage of the term 'mark' regarding what is not a mark, based on the commonality of the form of a mark,
Operates in a reversed manner. // 33 //
This has been stated in detail in the <s>Śrutiliṅgādhikaraṇa</s> (section on Vedic text and inferential marks);
Therefore, there is no deviation in both — the inferential and the scriptural [means of knowledge]. // 34 //
But is it not the case that meaning is first understood from human sentences,
For otherwise how could the speaker's specific cognition be inferred? // 35 //
For the specificity of cognitions lies only in their objects, since cognitions are formless (<s>nirākāra</s>);
And specificity cannot be established through an object that is not apprehended. // 36 //
Here we say: Due to the suspicion of unreliability, the object is not ascertained;
And what is not ascertained is not known — this much is established. // 37 //
However, even when the sentence-meaning is not known, when the group of words is heard,
A reflection arises in the intelligent listener of this kind: // 38 //
'This person utters words whose meanings are fit to be mutually connected;
He is trustworthy (<s>āpta</s>); therefore by him surely the connection of those meanings is known.' // 39 //
'He does not at any time intend to state unconnected meanings,
Nor meanings whose connection is not apprehended' — thus there is no fault whatsoever. // 40 //
But in this way, mounted on a horse, you have forgotten the horse!
Having set out to establish the authority of the Veda, you have abandoned it! // 41 //
For it is through the capacity known in ordinary usage that words in the Veda are illuminating;
And in ordinary usage, you have relied on understanding through the mode of inference (<s>liṅga</s>). // 42 //
But the resolution for this has been shown by the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) himself,
By demonstrating that words have a connection with meaning. // 43 //
For when it is established that words denote connected meanings (<s>anvitārthābhidhāyitva</s>),
The specific cognition of the speaker can be known, and not otherwise, since // 44 //

children.text: jñāteṣu hi padārtheṣu śrotā vaktari kalpayet /
children.translated_text: When the word-meanings are known, the listener would attribute to the speaker
The knowledge of their mutual connection, and not otherwise — thus it has been shown. // 45 //
The natural capacity (<s>śakti</s>) of words for their respective word-meanings is established;
In human sentences, it is concealed by the suspicion of unreliability. // 46 //
But in the Vedas, which have no remembered author, in their own nature,
Being free from contact with other means of knowledge for meaning-comprehension, // 47 //
There can be no inference of an author from the mark of sentence-hood;

children.text: na kartā śaknuyādvākyaṃ kartuṃ kārye hyalaukike // 48 //
children.translated_text: For an author would be unable to compose a sentence regarding a non-mundane (<s>alaukika</s>) object. // 48 //
Therefore, in the Veda, there is no suspicion of unreliability whatsoever;
Since it is a cause of certainty about the object, its contact with the object is established. // 49 //
Freed from the mire of defects of speech, having cleared the thicket of thorns of opposing arguments,
This path of reasoning (<s>Nītipatha</s>) has been laid out more excellently by <s>Śālikanātha</s>. // 50 //
Thus, in the <s>Prakaraṇapañcikā</s> composed by the illustrious <s>Mahāmahopādhyāya Śālikanātha Miśra</s>,
The second chapter called <s>Nītipatha</s> (Path of Reasoning)
Is completed. // 2 //
Now the third chapter called <s>Nayavīthī</s> (Avenue of Logic).
Statement of the subject-matter of the chapter:
To establish that all cognition here is indeed veridical (<s>yathārtha</s>),
The correct view of Guru <s>Prabhākara</s> is elucidated. // 1 //
There, the <s>pūrvapakṣa</s> (prior objection):
There, first, some persons of refined intellect said this:
Error (<s>bhrama</s>) and doubt (<s>sandeha</s>) — both these cognitions are not veridical (<s>ayathārtha</s>). // 2 //
'This is silver' — that cognition regarding a shell-piece,

children.text: sā cedyathārthā bhrāntitvaṃ tadā tasyāstu kīdṛśam // 3 //
children.translated_text: If it were veridical, then what kind of error would belong to it? // 3 //
When even a cognition that reflects the object as it actually exists is an error,
Then the nature of error would apply to all valid cognitions (<s>pramāṇas</s>). // 4 //
If error is the non-apprehension of distinction — no, that is not so,
Because error would then apply even in deep sleep (<s>suṣupti</s>), since all distinctions are not grasped there. // 5 //

children.text: bhūdāgrahe gṛhīte ca yadi syād bhramarūpatā /
children.translated_text: If there is the nature of error when something is grasped but distinction is not grasped,
Then the perception of mere generality from a distance would also be error. // 6 //
And if it is veridical perception, then even a sublating cognition (<s>bādhaka</s>) is not proper;
Through cognitions that grasp previously unknown distinctions, a sublating cognition would not arise. // 7 //
And let it also be considered how this cognition can be veridical,
For this cognition determines the shell to be silver. // 8 //

children.text: rajatatvaṃ na śukteśca rajatasya na śuktitā /
children.translated_text: Silver-ness does not belong to the shell, nor shell-ness to silver;
Their mutual difference has been ascertained through direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>). // 9 //
If this cognition does not apprehend the shell as silver,
Then the apprehension through co-referentiality (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) is contradicted. // 10 //
And the activity of one desiring silver toward the shell would be without basis;

children.text: agraho 'pi na bhedasya pravṛttau kāraṇaṃ yataḥ // 11 //
children.translated_text: Since even the non-apprehension of difference is not a cause of such activity. // 11 //
And this cognition of silver does not arise for a blind person;
Therefore it depends on the sense-organ; and if the sense-organ is in contact with the shell, the cognition // 12 //
Is capable of producing — and the sense-organ is in contact with the shell;
Therefore by the sense-organ itself, this [shell] is apprehended here as silver. // 13 //
One might think: only the shell is determined by the sense-organ;
That very shell, due to its similarity, is the cause of the memory of silver. // 14 //
Through the cognition of similarity, which causes the revival of the <s>saṃskāra</s> (mental impression),
There arises a memory of silver devoid of the reference 'that' [i.e., without the past-tense marker]. // 15 //
In this memory, due to a mental defect, the element 'that' referring to past experience is cut off;
Therefore, the conformity with the sense-organ is explained otherwise — and that is incorrect. // 16 //
Even regarding an experienced object, a cognition devoid of the reflective awareness of 'that'
Is not considered a genuine cognition or memory by them, like flowing-stream cognitions (<s>dhārāvāhika-bodha</s>). // 17 //
Because of the co-referentiality with something directly present and perceived,

children.text: neyaṃ smṛtiḥ, kintu śuktau bhrānto 'yaṃ rajatagrahaḥ // 18 //
children.translated_text: This is not memory; rather, this is an erroneous apprehension of silver in the shell. // 18 //
And in dreams there is nothing to serve as the cause for reviving memory;
And in the cognition of a yellow conch, and likewise in the perception of two moons — // 19 //
And the errors of directional confusion, whirling firebrand circles, and such —
How can these be explained as veridical by resorting to their being memory? // 20 //
Therefore, through defects of the sense-organs and such, erroneous cognitions arise,
Cognizing the real nature of the object otherwise than as it actually exists. // 21 //

children.text:
sthāṇurvā puruṣo veti sandeho yo 'pi jāyate /
abhāvāttadṛśo 'rthasya sa yathārthaḥ kathaṃ bhavet? // 22 //38 //
children.translated_text: And the doubt that arises — 'Is this a post or a person?' — since an object of such a kind does not exist, how can that be veridical? // 22 //
The <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion):

children.text: atra brūmo--ya evārtho yasyāṃ saṃvidi bhāsate /
children.translated_text: Here we say: Whatever object appears in whatever cognition,
That alone is what is to be known (<s>vedya</s>); for there is no other mark of what is to be known than being cognized. // 23 //
In 'this is silver,' silver indeed appears;

children.text: tadeva tena vedyaṃ syānna tu śuktiravedanāt // 24 //
children.translated_text: That alone would be what is known by it, but not the shell, since it is not cognized. // 24 //
Therefore, the appearance of one thing as another is refuted by the cognition itself;

children.text: parasmin bhāsamāne hi na paraṃ bhāsate yataḥ // 25 //
children.translated_text: For when one thing appears, another does not appear. // 25 //
But if so, how will this appearance of silver be explained?
It is said: the shell-piece is apprehended without its specific distinctions. // 26 //
The specific features of the shell that are the causes of distinction from silver

children.text: te na jñātā abhibhavād jñātā sāmānyarūpatā // 27 //
children.translated_text: Are not cognized due to being overpowered; only the generic form is cognized. // 27 //
And immediately after, a memory of silver arises; yet even so,
Due to a mental defect, it is devoid of the reflective awareness of the element 'that' (past reference). // 28 //
Having silver as its object, it does not discriminate the shell at all;
Therefore, the appearance of silver through memory will be well-established. // 29 //
And as for what was said — that this is not memory because it is like flowing-stream cognition —
It is replied: by the process of elimination, it must be memory, to make this understood here. // 30 //

children.text: na hyasannihitaṃ tāvat pratyakṣaṃ rajataṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: For, first, silver that is not present cannot be the object of direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>);
And due to the absence of inferential marks and such, it is not within the scope of another <s>pramāṇa</s>. // 31 //
By the process of elimination, it is memory — this certainty arises therefrom,
Because of the existence of its cause. But in flowing-stream cognitions, // 32 //
The assemblage of the present sense-organs serves as the cause of apprehension;
And these — apprehension and recollection — do not manifest their mutual distinction. // 33 //
Although truly different from the correct cognition of silver,
Yet since the difference does not appear, due to the equality of non-apprehension of difference, // 34 //
And the correct cognition of silver being a perception of the same single object,

children.text: tato bhinne abudhvā tu smaraṇagrahaṇe ime // 35 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, without cognizing the difference, these — memory and apprehension — // 35 //
Are merely considered by people as having the same form,
Due to the cognition having a directly present object and the apprehension having the same content. // 36 //
The cognition of non-difference — this much has been established;
And the corresponding behavior also proceeds from that very cognition. // 37 //
And due to the equality of cognition and due to the non-apprehension of difference,
Even the status of being false — because it occasions corresponding behavior — // 38 //

children.text:
rajatavyavahārāṃśe visaṃvādayato narān /
bādhakapratyayasyāpi bāndhakatvamato matam // 39 // (42)

children.translated_text: By preventing the silver-behavior that was about to occur. // 40 //
The sublating cognition (<s>bādhaka-pratyaya</s>) is also considered to be sublating precisely because it contradicts people regarding the silver-behavior portion. // 39 //
Just as a true cognition of silver arises regarding an actual silver piece that is present,
This erroneous cognition also shines forth in the same way, due to not determining the difference. // 41 //

children.text: sādhāraṇaṃ hi rūpaṃ tasyā asyāśca vidyate tena /
children.translated_text: For there exists a common form between that true cognition and this erroneous one; therefore,
From the appearance of only that common form, they consider them to be the same. // 42 //
Corresponding behavior and activity are also proper from this;
And the sublation by the sublating cognition operates by removing that behavior. // 43 //
Thus, in dreams too, objects that are being remembered indeed exist;
Through the concealment of the experienced portion, they appear as if being directly apprehended. // 44 //
For memory is a special case of apprehension — namely, the apprehension of what has already been apprehended;
Through the concealment of the apprehended portion, it stands as if it were direct apprehension. // 45 //
And <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit/demerit) is postulated as the cause for the revival of <s>saṃskāras</s> (impressions) there;
Even in the <s>viparītakhyāti</s> (erroneous cognition) view, this postulation is equally required. // 46 //
And since <s>adṛṣṭa</s> is the cause, such a cognition does not arise in a waking person;
For the condition of <s>adṛṣṭa</s> applies only when the assemblage of sense-organs can produce its result. // 47 //
And regarding the cognition of a yellow conch, the yellowness of bile (<s>pitta</s>) present in the sense-organ
Is apprehended, though devoid of a separate substance — like the sharpness perceived in water. // 48 //
And due to the defect of the sense-organ, the whiteness of the conch is not apprehended;
Only the bare substance shines forth, devoid of its actual color. // 49 //

children.text: guṇe dravyavyapekṣa45 ca dravye ca guṇakāṅkṣiṇi /
children.translated_text: And since a quality (<s>guṇa</s>) requires a substance (<s>dravya</s>), and a substance expects a quality,
When both appear, the cognition does not apprehend their non-connection. // 50 //
Through the appearance of real yellowness, these two cognitions being equal,
The corresponding behavior is also similar — thus this applies here as well. // 51 //
But as for the fact that the blackness of collyrium (<s>kajjala</s>) present in the eye is also not apprehended,
The reason for that is the obstruction of the sense-organ by it. // 52 //
That which is the orb of the eye, resembling an <s>atasī</s> (flax) flower,
and the collyrium (<s>añjana</s>) situated therein, which obstructs the function of the visual faculty — [53]
But the collyrium that is situated within the inner circle of the eye,
its dark blueness is not perceived due to the defect of its non-straightness (obliqueness). [54]
Even though smeared on the upper part of the sense-organ, due to its transparent nature,

children.text: pittena nāyanaṃ tejaḥ kāceneva na ruddhyate // 55 //
children.translated_text: the visual fire is not obstructed by bile, just as [it is not obstructed] by glass. [55]
The visual fire, as it extends outward, is the apprehender; it is not situated in the sense-organ alone.
The non-apprehension of bile is due to its subtlety, like the non-apprehension of fire in its radiance. [56]
The cognition of bitterness in what is sweet is thus explained for one free from [excess] bile,
through the acceptance that the bitterness is devoid of [real] taste, and [the acceptance] of jaggery [as truly sweet]. [57]
Similarly, even in the perception of two moons, the visual radiance, divided twofold by a split in the sense-organ,
produces [the appearance of two] in the one moon itself, whose luminosity is divided. [58]

children.text: samvittī te na bhidyete taddvitve sati manyate /
children.translated_text: Those two cognitions are not actually distinct; when there is such duality, it is merely thought to be so.
Even here, the equality with cognition of distinct objects is indeed as before. [59]
Even though one remembers the oneness [of the moon], this error is accounted for by that explanation.

children.text: na hi smṛtipramoṣeṇa sarvatraiva bhramo mataḥ // 60 //
children.translated_text: For error is not regarded everywhere as merely a lapse of memory. [60]
In the delusion of directions, due to the unseen power [of past impressions] and the non-apprehension of the true nature of directions,
and from the remembrance of the form of another direction — the error is explained. [61]
In the fire-wheel illusion, when the firebrand revolves rapidly in all directions,
the cognitions that arise without interruption are regarded as equivalent to the cognition of a wheel. [62]

children.text:
kālabhedastu śīghratvāddhiyāṃ tāsāṃ na lakṣyate /
cakradhīvyavahāraśca tenāsminnapi yujyate // 63 // 48//
children.translated_text: But the temporal difference of those cognitions is not noticed due to their rapidity; and therefore the practical usage of 'wheel-cognition' is fitting even in this case. [63]
In this very manner, by the learned, in all cases of error,
the distinctions of causes should be reasoned out for establishing veridical knowledge. [64]

children.text: sthāṇurvā puruṣo veti sandehe 'pi yadā dvayam /
children.translated_text: Even in doubt, such as 'Is this a post or a man?', when both alternatives
are remembered as mutually exclusive, how can there be absence of an object? [65]
And if some cognition arises while abandoning the object,
being deviant regarding its own object, how can it be a cause of confidence? [66]
But here too, the answer is the same as the suspicion of equivalence with the silver-cognition [in shell-silver].
If the determination is sought — there is no distrust there, due to the absence of defect. [67]
This objection equally applies even in the theory of <s>viparītakhyāti</s> (erroneous apprehension).
Alas! How great is this negligence even of the wise! [68]
For when cognition is deviant, on what basis does confidence rest?

children.text: jñānasya vyabhicāre 'pi jñātaṃ yat satyameva tat // 69 //
children.translated_text: Even when cognition is deviant, what is known is indeed real. [69]
But there is also ignorance, which is based on the distinction of forms.
This desire to know that arises — that too is removed by another cognition. [70]

children.text:
yatnenānviṣyamāṇe 'pi rūpaṃ taccenna dṛśyate /
tadā pūrvaiva saṃvittista49 ttvenāpyapadiśyate // 71 // 50//
children.translated_text: Even when sought with effort, if that form is not seen, then the prior cognition itself is designated as true. [71]

children.text:
ayathārthatvapakṣe ca jñānaṃ sākāramāpatet /
ākāro bhāsate yo hi jñāna evāvatiṣṭhate // 72 // 51//
children.translated_text: And in the view of non-veridicality, cognition would turn out to possess a form; for the form that appears indeed resides in cognition alone. [72]

children.text:
ayathārthasya bodhasya notpattāvasti kāraṇam /
doṣāścenna hi doṣāṇāṃ kāryaśaktivighātitā // 73 // 52//
children.translated_text: There is no cause for the arising of non-veridical cognition — unless defects are posited; but the capacity of defects to produce effects is refuted. [73]
In cases of <s>bhasmaka</s> (digestive disorder) and the like, the defective nature is established precisely from the obstruction of the normal effect.
For the production of taste is the effect of the fire residing in the stomach. [74]
The obstructive nature of defects consists in blocking the apprehension of the form of the existing object.
Thus the error of defects is established as being rooted in non-apprehension. [75]
To establish the non-deviation with respect to objects of all cognitions, this
<s>Nayavīthī</s> (Path of Reasoning) was composed by <s>Śālikanātha</s>, the knower of logic. [76]
By <s>Miśra Śālikanātha</s>, the treatise named <s>Nayavīthī</s>
was composed for the welfare of the world, in accordance with the doctrine of <s>Prabhākara</s>. [77]

children.text: iti śrīmahāmahopādhyāya-śālikanāthamiśrapraṇītāyāṃ prakaraṇapañcikāyāṃ nītipatho nāma tṛtīyaṃ prakaraṇaṃ samāptam //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third chapter named <s>Nītipatha</s> (Path of Reasoning) in the <s>Prakaraṇapañcikā</s> composed by the illustrious <s>Mahāmahopādhyāya Śālikanātha Miśra</s>.
The fourth chapter named <s>Jātinirṇaya</s> (Determination of Universals).
Statement of the subject-matter of the chapter —
In many ways
the learned dispute regarding <s>jāti</s> (universals).
According to the doctrine of <s>Prabhākara</s>, this refutation of those views is stated. [1]

children.text:
kecidācakṣate jātiriti vikalpavilāsitam iti /
eke tu sattīmapi jātimāśrayebhyo 'bhinnāmanumanyante /
anye tu bhinnāmapyanumeyāmāhuḥ /

children.translated_text: Still others hold it to be both distinct and non-distinct from its substrata.

children.text: tathā ajātāvapi jātivyavahāro bahulamupalabhyate keṣāñciditi tannirākaraṇāyedamārabhyate /
children.translated_text: Similarly, since for some the usage of <s>jāti</s> is abundantly found even where no real universal exists, this discussion is undertaken to refute that.
The established conclusion (<s>siddhānta</s>): <s>Jāti</s> (universal) is distinct from its substrata and is an object of perceptual knowledge.
This is the view of Guru <s>Prabhākara</s>, established through the reflection on prior cognized forms. [2]

Some declare that <s>jāti</s> (universal) is merely a play of conceptual construction. Others, however, accept <s>jāti</s> as real but identical with its substrata. Yet others maintain that it is distinct from substrata but only inferable.

children.text:
pūrvapakṣaḥ- nanvāśraya eva dravyaṃ jāterasaditi saugatāḥ /
tathāhi na paramāṇuṣu caturvidheṣu pārthivāpyataijasavāyavīyeṣu jātirāśritābhimatā, anuvṛttākārapratyayaviyogāt /
bhinneṣu yadabhinnā jātirupeyate, tatrānuvṛttākārāvabhāsinī buddhireva nibandhanam /
na kasyacijjantoḥ paramāṇuṣu karaṇapathavidūravartiṣu nipuṇamapi nirūpayo 'nuvṛttākārāvabhāsino matirāvirbhavati /
yāpi ceyaṃ paramāṇuriti matiḥ, sāpi 56pārimāṇḍalyalakṣaṇaguṇakāraṇikā mīmāṃsakairapi saṅgīryate /
pṛthivītvādikamapi na tattadasādhāraṇagandhādiguṇasamavāyamātralabdhātmalābhāyāṃ pṛthivyādibuddhau nibandhanam /
na ca sthaleṣu dravyeṣa jātiḥ samaveyāt, teṣāmeva durupagamatvāt /
na khalu sthūladravyārambho57 ghaṭate /
tathā hi---dvyaṇukādikrameṇa sthūladravyārambho 'bhidhīyate, tatra tāvad dravyārambha eva na sādhīyāniti manyāmahe /
na khalu tathaivaikaḥ paramāṇurārabhate /
dravyasyaikākinaḥ sthūladravyāntarārambhakatvānupapatteḥ /
na caikaikadravyavyatiriktamaparamārambhakamasti /
saṃyogo 'pi ca tayoranupapanna eva /
sa hi naikaikadravyasamavetaḥ, nāpyanekadravyasamavetaḥ /
ekaikātirekeṇānekasyābhāvāt /
evañca pratyekamekadravyasamavetatvābhāve, nānekadravyasamavetatvamapi sambhavati /
anenaiva mārgeṇa tryaṇukasya trimirdvyaṇukairārambhaṇīyasya mahimaguṇaśālinaḥ sambhavo nirastaḥ /
tadevaṃ dūrabhūtā sthavīyasāmavayavināmārambhasaṃkathā /
api cāvayavinaḥ kimavayaveṣu pratyekaṃ kārtsnyena vṛttiḥ ? vyāsaṅgena vā ? iti cintanīyam /
na tāvat kārtsnyena vṛttimupalabhāmahe, ekaikāvayavagatasya tasyāpratipatteḥ /
ekaikāvayavagate ca kampe rāge vā sakalasyāvayavinaḥ kamparāgapratītiprasaṅgāt /
tathāvayavāntare ca kamparāgavirahe kamparāgavirahasamāsakteḥ, avayavī kampeta na kampeta, rajyeta na rajyeta ceti viṣamāṃ daśāmāviśet /
nāpi vyāsaṅgenāvayavino vṛttiravayavāntaravirahāt /
avayavāntaraśālino hi kenacidavayavena kvacana, kenacidavayavena kvacaneti vyāsaṅginī vṛttirupapattimatī /
kiñcaikaikatrāvṛtteravṛttireva, ekaikātiriktānekābhāvāt /
kiñca sakalāvayavagrahaṇe eva niyamenāvayavī jñāyeta, na ca tathā sambhavati, avayavāntareṇāvayavāntaratiraskārāt /
na ca prakārāntareṇa vṛttiriti vadituṃ śakyam; anupapatteḥ prakārāntarasya /
avayavebhyaścāvayavī vyatiricyamāno 'vyatiricyamāno vā na pramāṇena saṅgacchate /
vyatirikto hi digrahe 'pi grahaṇaṃ kadācidanubhavet /
na khalu bhinnayoḥ sahopalambhaniyamo ghaṭapaṭayoriva /
tadvadavayavyapi bhidyamāno nāvayavaireva sahopalabhyeta /
kasyāñcidapi daśāyāmananubhūyamāneṣvapyavayaveṣvanubhūyeta /
na cāvayavinamavayavānubhavamantareṇa kecidupalabhante /
avyatiricyamānastu nāstyeveti vacanabhaṅgimātreṇoktaṃ bhavati /
tadevamavayavi dravyamupapattibhiranusandhīyamānamekāntato līyate /
kathaṃ tarhi sthūlāvabhāsinī manīṣā samarthanīyā ? ittham--uttarādharabhāvena nirantaramutpannāḥ paramāṇava eva samadhigataindriyakajñānajananayogyadaśāviśeṣāḥ pratyakṣamīkṣyante /
tāṃstathābhūtānanusaṃdadhatastadbalabhāvī mānasa eva sthūlavikalpo vijṛmbhate, dūrādiva taruṣu nirantareṣu samanubhūyamāneṣu vanamiti matiḥ /
ataḥ sthavīyasāṃ dravyāṇāmāśrayatvenābhimatānāmayogājjātirapi tadāśritā nābhyupagamamarhati /
api ca jātirapi nendriyajñānaviṣayā pratīyate, tasyā nityatvenābhyupagamāt /
nahi nityaṃ kasmaicitkāryāya paryāptam; taddhi na śaktasvabhāvam, nityaṃ kāryodayaprasaṅgāt /
aśaktasvabhāvaṃ tu nityatvādavicikitsayāśaktikaṃ nityaṃ na kiñcit kuryāt /
na cājanakamindiranayajñānaviṣayatāmanubhavati /
yo hi viṣayaḥ svasyānvayavyatirekajñānamanukārayati, sa pratyakṣaḥ /
kiñca samunmiṣitacakṣuṣaścirāya viṣayāntarānusandhānavyāvṛttacittasya purovartinīṃ svastimatīṃ kālākṣīṃ vā sākṣātkurvāṇasyeva na jātiraparāvabhāsate /
anyacca na jātirasau piṇḍaiḥ sahotpadyate, vinaśyati vā /
tathopagame 58svarūpahāniprasaṅgāt /
ekā59 ca jātiranekādhiṣṭhānā pratijñāyate, utpattimatī vināśinī cānyānyā syāt, viruddhadharmādhyāsasya bhedāpādakatvāt /
seyaṃ nityā jātiruditavatyāṃ vyaktau pratīyamānā nānyata āgatā, niṣkriyatvāt /
na ca tatraivāsīt, prāgapratīteḥ /
na ca sthitirapi yuktimatī, vyaktireva hi tasyā deśo nākāśādiḥ, anutpannā ca vyaktiriti kvāvatiṣṭhatāmākṛtiḥ /
nacotpādye 'pyavatiṣṭhate /
tadeṣā jātiravatiṣṭhate, nāvatiṣṭhate ca, iti saṅkaṭamāpatitam /
kiñca vyakterabhinnā vā ?bhinnā vā ? ubhayarūpā vā jātirāstheyā ? /

children.translated_text: But this [cognition of sameness] is explained by non-apprehension of difference, like the cognition of silver in a shell — so it does not suffice to establish a universal (<s>sāmānya</s>).
