children.translated_text: For being a recipient of the fruit produced by action (<s>kriyājanyaphalabhāgitā</s>), being invariable everywhere, is what is to be denoted by the accusative case (<s>dvitīyā</s>), not subordination (<s>śeṣitā</s>), because of [the latter's] variability.
The <s>kāraka</s> that participates in the fruit produced by the action is indeed the <s>karma</s> (object).
And some of that is desired (<s>īpsita</s>), because of its usefulness for what already exists and what is to come into being.
And some is undesired (<s>anīpsita</s>), because of its lack of usefulness.

Thus. The definition of cooperative subsidiaries (<s>sannipātī aṅga</s>). What then is the definition of the cooperative assistance of all four [types of subsidiaries]? That which produces its fruit dependent on a particular injunction of causal factors — that is the cooperative subsidiary. For example: bathing for the agent, threshing (<s>avaghāta</s>) and such for the object, bringing curds for the location — and so on, which should be reasoned out. Doubt according to the <s>Bhāṭṭa</s> view: Among those, in the sentences regarding cooperative subsidiaries, some accept separate injunctions. For they think: If separate injunctions are not accepted here, then the subsidiary status of threshing and such with respect to the eligibility-injunction would not obtain. Nor can subsidiary status be established through the connection with the eligibility-injunction's <s>apūrva</s> by means of connection with the substance, since words like '<s>vrīhi</s>' (rice) denote the generic form (<s>ākṛti</s>). Even though the word for the universal, by virtue of the individual's proximity to the effect, indicates the individual, still only the bare individual is indicated, not the individual connected with a specific <s>apūrva</s>. Nor can the connection with <s>apūrva</s> be established through the indication of the individual that is a means to the <s>apūrva</s> of that [eligibility-injunction], as in the <s>Āgneyī</s> principle; for even though by the <s>Āgneyī</s> principle there is the inclusion of the individual that is present, their cognition is through their bare form alone, excluding individuals not relevant, and not as means to a specific <s>apūrva</s>, since that bare form is merely indicative (<s>lākṣaṇika</s>). And there is no cause for indication-of-what-is-indicated (<s>lakṣitalakṣaṇā</s>). For thus: the individual is indicated by the universal, and the specific means by the individual — this indication-of-what-is-indicated is improper due to the absence of a cause. Hence, in '<s>āgneyā agnīdhram upatiṣṭhate</s>' ('One approaches the fire-altar with the <s>āgneyī</s> [offering]') [<s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 3.1.6], even though inclusion of the relevant [offering] obtains, the fire-altar is not approached with another ritual act. And hence there is no contradiction with the assignment. Since the approaching of the fire-altar is not assigned as a means to another effect, and thus — since the connection of threshing and such is merely through their bare form, the establishment of connection with a specific <s>apūrva</s> is not achieved, like the restriction of speech (<s>vāṅniyama</s>) of the <s>dīkṣaṇīyā</s>. Just as the restriction of speech, through its connection with its own subordinate <s>apūrva</s>, does not enter into the eligibility-<s>apūrva</s>, so too would threshing and such. And hence, the subsidiary status of threshing and such with respect to the eligibility-<s>apūrva</s> would not obtain. And in the absence of subsidiary status, since there would be no prompting through it, the performance of threshing and such would not occur. Therefore, a production-injunction (<s>utpattiniyoga</s>) for threshing and such must be accepted. When that is resorted to, since its performance is impossible without eligibility, when an eligible person must be postulated, the very person eligible for the eligibility-<s>apūrva</s> is also made eligible for the subsidiary rites like <s>prayāja</s> and such — and thus, through the relation of means and end, the establishment of their subsidiary status [is achieved]. Refutation of this: The venerable Teacher (<s>Prabhākara</s>) does not approve of this. Hence he says, at [<s>Bṛhatṭīkā</s> 3.1.3]: 'You are unaware of the nature of the object and the person enjoined.' In the case of threshing and such, through the word and through the nature of things, the visible effect such as the removal of husks and particles is [accepted]; in sprinkling (<s>prokṣaṇa</s>) and such, through the word alone, an unseen effect too is accepted. Now, if in that case another <s>niyoga</s> is also resorted to as the effect, then two effects cannot be connected in a single sentence. Nor can this [<s>niyoga</s>] be like the fruit such as heaven and such — since the fruit is connected as a qualifier of the person enjoined. And the removal of husks and such is not a qualifier of the person enjoined, being the fruit of the action. Only what is the fruit of the <s>niyoga</s> can serve as the qualifier of the person enjoined. For the person enjoined, qualified by what is to be accomplished, can accept as duty only that which accomplishes what is to be accomplished for him — thus the establishment of the qualifier of the person enjoined is ascertained. And what is the fruit of action — that is not accomplished through <s>niyoga</s>, so the one qualified by that does not attain the status of being enjoined in the <s>niyoga</s>. Nor is it proper to abandon the cognized effect of removal of husks and such, due to the very impropriety of abandoning what is cognized. [Objection:] But by the force of the employment of <s>liṅ</s> and such which denote <s>niyoga</s>, <s>niyoga</s> too is cognized — so the fault is equal. It is replied: When an injunction is present in proximity, that very injunction being cognized is first proper to be understood. If the object does not enter into the scope of that injunction, then there would be another injunction. And threshing and such do enter into the scope of the relevant object, due to their connection with rice and such which serve that purpose. Through the words like '<s>avahanti</s>' (they thresh), threshing and such are expressed with the purport of serving the proximate eligibility-injunction, since those [acts] of that nature are instructed in the relation of action and causal factor. If the connection were with rice and such in their bare form alone, then there would be no connection with the eligibility of that [injunction]; hence, through the indication of the specific means-nature by words like '<s>vrīhi</s>' and such, threshing and such, presented by words like '<s>avahanti</s>', are connected — not the bare form. And thus, through instruction alone, threshing is established even in the case of barley (<s>yava</s>), since there is no distinction in the means-nature. And hence threshing and such, being already obtained (<s>prāpta</s>) as means of <s>niyoga</s>, are enjoined [merely for restriction]. But restriction is the purpose. If threshing and such were not enjoined as subsidiaries of <s>niyoga</s>, then even splitting with nails and such would be drawn in for the mere accomplishment of the rice-cake (<s>puroḍāśa</s>). But when threshing and such are enjoined as subsidiaries of <s>niyoga</s>, since the accomplishment of <s>niyoga</s> is impossible without them, they are restrictively [enjoined] — nothing else is drawn in. But subsidiary status with respect to <s>niyoga</s> is itself unobtained even on the other view, since <s>niyoga</s>, being supra-mundane, its subsidiary status too cannot be known from anything other than the word. And since threshing and such are subsidiaries of <s>niyoga</s>, the connection of <s>niyoga</s> with what is already obtained is restated by <s>liṅ</s> and such. Doubt and resolution regarding whether threshing and such are objects of <s>niyoga</s>: [Objection:] If threshing and such have a connection with <s>niyoga</s>, how then is it said that they are not objects of <s>niyoga</s>? It is said thus: It is not mere connection with <s>niyoga</s> that is being discussed. One whose very effect is the accomplishment of <s>niyoga</s> — that is the object. But threshing and such, while producing the intermediate effect of removal of husks and particles, are not objects of <s>niyoga</s>. Therefore, their non-object-status with respect to <s>niyoga</s>, and their subsidiary status — both are established. And threshing and such are to be enjoined, since they are employed for the accomplishment of <s>niyoga</s>. As it is said: 'What is employed for the accomplishment of that — that is to be enjoined: this is the usage in the system' [Commentary, p. 39]. Thus, through mere proximity strengthened by the recognition of <s>niyoga</s>, the subsidiary status of threshing and such with respect to <s>niyoga</s> [is established], not through the connection of word-meanings — this is established. But for those who accept entry through the connection of word-meanings, since there is no distinction between the fifteen-versed [<s>sāmidhenī</s>] studied within the context and the seventeen-versed studied outside the context — both entering through the connection with <s>sāmidhenī</s> — both would be placed in the model rite (<s>prakṛti</s>) alone, and there would be an option. But when through mere proximity the contextually studied [fifteen-versed] is accepted, since the fifteen-versed quickly enters the eligibility [of the model rite], when that is appropriated, the seventeen-versed, being contradicted by the eligibility, does not enter. Therefore, it is placed in the modified rite (<s>vikṛti</s>) alone. If through proximity there is entry into the eligibility-injunction, then how is the entry of <s>parṇatā</s> (leaf-ness) and such, which are studied outside the context, [explained]? It is replied: <s>Juhu</s> (ladle) and such have an invariable connection with the ritual; through that connection, the connection with the ritual is established, and in the <s>juhu</s> and such that are thus connected, the connection with leaf-ness and such [is established]. Hence, '<s>hiraṇyaṃ bhāryām</s>' ('gold, a wife') [<s>Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa</s> 2.2.5.2] is independently an object of the eligibility-injunction, since gold deviates from the connection with the ritual. And for those who, [arguing] that mere connection with the bare word-meaning would lead to purposelessness, assert connection through the relational state followed by the grasper-connection — for them, this very point [needs to be explained]: how can there not be purposelessness? If [it is argued] 'because it is a Vedic sentence' — there is no royal decree that a Vedic sentence must not be purposeless. For that whose meaning is understood, let there be no purposelessness; but for that whose meaning is not ascertained, the purposefulness is a mere mental fabrication. Since purposefulness can be achieved even by resorting to another position, it is better to accept the subsidiary status with respect to <s>niyoga</s> through mere proximity. For those learned in sentence-meaning [say]: 'Proximity too is a cause of connection.' And connection cannot exist without the relation of subordinate and principal (<s>guṇapradhānabhāva</s>). And there, since 'an effect does not serve another purpose,' <s>niyoga</s> alone is the principal, and threshing and such are the subsidiaries. Doubt and resolution regarding the scope of proximity: If purposelessness [leads to] connection with <s>niyoga</s>, then '<s>tṛca uttamaḥ paryāsaḥ</s>' ('the triple verse is the highest rearrangement') would not be placed in the twelve-day rite (<s>dvādaśāha</s>) alone. For the inner rearrangement (<s>antaḥparyāsa</s>) is said to be connected with the ritual. Therefore, even with mere connection of word-meaning, there is no purposelessness there. Similarly, '<s>hiraṇmayyaḥ sruco bhavanti</s>' ('the ladles should be golden') [<s>Āpastamba Śrautasūtra</s> 8.5.29] — since ladles have an invariable connection with the ritual, there would be no purposelessness of the quality-injunction, so the connection with the eligibility of the model rite would not follow. Moreover, connection with <s>apūrva</s> was accepted to avoid purposelessness. Why not resort to the connection with the proximate <s>apūrva</s>? If proximity is not a cause, then '<s>agnes tṛṇāny apacinoti</s>' ('one gathers the grasses of the fire') [<s>Āpastamba Śrautasūtra</s> 3.4.3] would not be restricted to the <s>Agnihotra</s> alone. If through specific proximity the fire and such connected with that <s>apūrva</s> are accepted, then let the connection with that <s>apūrva</s> itself be through specific proximity — what need of resorting to indirect [connection]? Just as connected denotation operates through the relation of action and causal factor, so too through the relation of purpose and purposeful (<s>prayojana-prayojanibhāva</s>), denotation is understood in the world. Since rice and such do not deserve the status of purpose, setting them aside, the connection with <s>apūrva</s> alone through the relation of purpose and purposeful [is established]. Doubt and resolution regarding intermediate <s>apūrva</s>: For those who assert intermediate <s>apūrva</s>s in threshing and such — in their view, in '<s>prokṣitābhyām ulūkhala-musalābhyām avahanti</s>' ('they thresh with sprinkled mortar and pestle'), the sprinkling would be prompted by the intermediate <s>apūrva</s>, like the restriction of speech of the <s>dīkṣaṇīyā</s>. And hence, like the restriction of speech in the <s>Traidhātavīya</s>, sprinkling would not occur in a cake split by nails, since the prompting form is not present there. Nor should it be said that through the effect of removal of husks and such, the eligibility-<s>apūrva</s> itself is the prompter — since the same consequence would follow for the restriction of speech too, for even in the <s>dīkṣaṇīyā</s> there is an effect required by the ritual, so the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s> alone would be the prompter of the restriction of speech. And hence it would apply even in the <s>Traidhātavīya</s> which produces the state of being initiated. [Objection:] If intermediate injunctions are not accepted in threshing and such, how then does the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> (<s>Śabara</s>) accept intermediate injunctions specifically for subsidiaries, in saying 'what is not enjoined is not a subsidiary' [<s>Śābarabhāṣya</s> 3.4.13]? It is replied: The intermediate injunction is accepted for remote-assisting [subsidiaries] and for the prohibition of untruth, since without them subsidiary status would not be established. Since ritual actions are momentary in nature and do not persist at the time of producing assistance, subsidiary status would not be established — we shall state this here itself. Hence, in the case of a cooperative subsidiary like the <s>jajjabhya</s> mantra-recitation, the <s>Bhāṣyakāra</s> says: 'The hearing of personal effort is a restatement.' For where there is an intermediate injunction, the hearing of personal effort is not a restatement. For that very intermediate <s>apūrva</s> is the effect to be denoted by <s>liṅ</s> and such. And since without denoting the personal effort in the form of the act (<s>kṛti</s>), the denotation of an effect whose nature is delimited by the act is not possible — hence the denotation of personal effort in the form of the act is proper, so personal effort is not unintended. Thus, through mere proximity strengthened by the recognition of <s>niyoga</s> and the tradition, threshing and such, expressed by words like '<s>avahanti</s>', are understood as connected with the eligibility-injunction in the capacity of serving it, and being connected through the relation of action and causal factor with rice and such in their means-related state, they attain subsidiary status with respect to those [rice and such]. Statement of the probative force of <s>śruti</s> and such according to his own view: What then is the <s>pramāṇa</s> for the subsidiary status of threshing with respect to rice and such? We say: it is the effect (<s>kārya</s>). For thus: an effect does not serve another purpose, by virtue of being an effect. Therefore, what is connected with an effect — that much serves the purpose of that [effect]. And what is connected with something that has assumed the purposefulness of the effect — with that too, what has the relation of means and end serves that purpose alone, since there is no <s>pramāṇa</s> for the purposefulness of what has assumed the purposefulness of the effect having a different purposefulness. Thus, the subordinate-principal relation should be understood in all cases. If the purposefulness is understood through duty-ness alone, how then is the causal role of <s>śruti</s> (direct statement) and such in assignment? Through presenting specific means. And the subsidiary attains subsidiary status with respect to the principal by being a specifier of the effect, not otherwise, since subsidiary status of what is ineffective is impossible. There, <s>śruti</s> (direct statement), in the form of the accusative case in '<s>vrīhīn avahanti</s>' ('they thresh the rice-grains'), presenting the effect to be accomplished by the threshing connected with the rice — namely the removal of husks and such — restates the instrumentality of <s>niyoga</s>. The mere accusative case does not establish the principal status of rice and such, or the subsidiary status of threshing — since there is deviation in '<s>gāṃ dadāti</s>' ('he gives a cow') and similar [expressions where the accusative does not indicate the principal-subsidiary relation].

children.translated_text: And it is possible here for the unity of <s>niyoga</s> to be [maintained] through the processing of its rice grains — thus it has been stated.
For if the equality of threshing and such with the <s>prayājas</s> were accepted, another production-<s>niyoga</s> would have to be resorted to — this we shall state.
Summary verses thereon: Arisen by the force of proximity, leading to the principal <s>apūrva</s>,
'Do not obstruct the recognition' — with the desire for its assistance. [3]

By this very distinction, the revered <s>Pāṇini</s>'s two <s>sūtras</s> — '<s>karturīpsitatamaṃ karma</s>' [<s>Pāṇini Sūtra</s> 1.4.49] and '<s>tathāyuktañcānīpsitam</s>' [<s>Pāṇini Sūtra</s> 1.4.50]. In the view of those who hold that the meaning of the accusative is subordination (<s>śeṣitā</s>) alone, in their view '<s>suvarṇaṃ bhāryām</s>' (gold as wife) would be a property of the ritual (<s>kratu</s>) alone. For only entry into a qualification concordant with what is heard is proper, not the postulation of an independent qualification, because of the unwanted consequence of abandoning the already-known subordination of gold. But when the meaning of the word is being-a-recipient-of-the-fruit-produced-by-action, there is no abandonment of what is heard, and since the independent agent is understood, the postulation of the qualification that is its cause is alone proper. Because the principal <s>niyoga</s> is not recognized, when one is situated in another <s>niyoga</s>, the postulation of qualification — like the postulation of qualification in the <s>Prajāpati-vrata</s> — alone is fitting. An example of indicative sign (<s>liṅga</s>): In bathing and such, through the examination of the intrinsic nature of things, from the indicative sign, the acceptance of the <s>kārya</s> in the form of purification of the agent is established. Thereby, the subordination of bathing and such to the agent is [established] through capacity (<s>sāmarthya</s>). And mere capacity is the indicative sign, not the capacity of designation alone. An example of sentence (<s>vākya</s>) [as a means of assignment]: In [sentences like] '<s>abhikrāmaṃ juhoti</s>' [<s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 2.6.6.1] and such, from the sentence, stepping forward is understood as having oblation as its purpose — thus this assignment is through the sentence. But for elements that help through combination (<s>sannipattyupakāraka</s>), assignment through context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) is not possible. For those for which context provides the means, their assignment depends on context. Examination of context (<s>prakaraṇa</s>): Context is the expectancy of the procedure (<s>itikartavyatā</s>). And through that, the instrumental helpfulness, being what is to be accomplished, is postulated. And that is not the means for elements that help through combination — hence there is no assignment of those through context. Position (<s>sthāna</s>) and nomenclature (<s>samākhyā</s>) do not have the capacity to assign the combination-helping elements. Position and nomenclature also do not postulate the <s>kārya</s> with respect to combination-helping elements — hence they are not causes of assignment. Thus, for combination-helping elements, the purpose-relation with <s>niyoga</s> is through designation (<s>abhidhāna</s>), the purpose-relation with <s>kāraka</s> is through assignment (<s>viniyoga</s>), and the purpose-relation with the sacrifice and such that become the instrument of the qualification-<s>niyoga</s> is through proximate mention (<s>upādāna</s>). For <s>upādāna</s> (proximate mention) is the indication of <s>niyoga</s>; through that, the purpose-relation of sprinkling (<s>prokṣaṇa</s>) and such with the ritual is established. If the instrumental helpfulness belonging to it did not pertain to sprinkling and such, then by what other means would the cognition of <s>niyoga</s> connected with that be sustained — thus, the <s>niyoga</s> itself, being cognized as connected with that, postulating its instrumental helpfulness, indicates the purpose-relation with the instrument — hence the purpose-relation of sprinkling and such with the ritual is established precisely through that. But since through assignment there is only the purpose-relation with <s>kāraka</s>, how then is their instrumental helpfulness [established]? Through conferring a specific quality upon what is to be helped, by means of a chain of effects such as the removal of husks and grains. But if so, for those that enter as <s>kārakas</s>, like the threshing (<s>avaghāta</s>) and such, the instrumental helpfulness is through conferring a specific quality upon the body of the instrument, while for the <s>prayājas</s> and such, it is through generating the favor of a distinct instrument — hence not all of them produce the same kind of help. And therefore, the principle that 'all belong to the same procedure' would not hold. We reply: Since the accomplishment of help depends on a specific entity to be helped, the specific entity to be helped is capable of producing help only for it and not for another — this is understood from the assignment of threshing and such. And thus it is established that even the threshing and such, together with the <s>prayājas</s>, produce instrumental helpfulness. Doubt and refutation regarding whether combination-elements help from afar: Why then are the threshing and such not accepted as helpers like the <s>prayājas</s>? Because of the recognition of the principal qualification-<s>niyoga</s>.
Through words like '<s>avahanti</s>' (he threshes) and such, whose word-meanings are connected with the <s>kārya</s>,
their own meaning is designated as connected with the principal <s>apūrva</s> alone. [4]
That being so, for one wishing to preserve their belonging to it [the principal <s>niyoga</s>],
connected with words like 'rice' and such, the characteristic of being a means to the <s>kārya</s> [is established]. [5]
The relation of action and <s>kāraka</s> too is therefore within the scope of the means.
The principal-status (<s>śeṣibhāva</s>) too belongs to that alone, following the Vedic means. [6]

Thus, in the <s>Prakaraṇapañcikā</s> composed by the illustrious <s>Mahāmahopādhyāya Śrīmac-Śālikanātha Miśra</s>, in the <s>Aṅgapārāyaṇa</s> (Examination of Subsidiary Elements), the first section (<s>pariccheda</s>) dealing with the examination of combination-helping subsidiary elements (<s>sannipattyupakārakāṅga</s>) is concluded.
[Chapter 13, Section 2]
Now, in the <s>Aṅgapārāyaṇa</s> (Examination of Subsidiary Elements), [begins] the [section] dealing with the examination of subsidiary elements that help from afar (<s>ārādupakārakāṅga</s>).

children.translated_text: Determination of incidental application (<s>prasaṅga</s>):

children.text: yasya ca parārthamanuṣṭhitasyāpi kāryaṃ tantramityavagamyate, tasyānyatrāpyupakārakatvameveti sakṛdanuṣṭhānam--iti /
children.translated_text: And for one whose rite, even though performed for another's benefit, is understood to have the obligatory (<s>tantra</s>) as its purpose — his performance elsewhere too is recognized as beneficial, and therefore it is performed only once.
For those whose limbs are immersed in the ocean of injunctions, subject to manifold delusions,
this traversal has been accomplished of those [topics] that are vast and deep.

The remote auxiliary (<s>ārādupakāraka</s>) is of two kinds: that which has an unseen purpose (<s>adṛṣṭaprayojana</s>), and that which has a seen-and-unseen purpose (<s>dṛṣṭādṛṣṭaprayojana</s>). Of these, an example of one with unseen purpose is 'He sacrifices with firewood (<s>samidaḥ</s>)' [<s>Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa</s> 2.6.1.1] and the like. No purpose pertaining to its causal factors is observed. A partisan view regarding the domain of remote auxiliaries: Some hold that for the purpose of establishing the subsidiary status of these [auxiliaries], they wish them to have qualification-dependent qualification (<s>adhikṛtādhikāra</s>) with respect to the qualification-related unprecedented merit (<s>adhikārāpūrva</s>). For they think: the injunctions of production (<s>utpattiniyoga</s>) regarding firewood and the like are undisputedly accepted. And an injunction is not expressed without an enjoinee (<s>niyojya</s>). This being so, the postulation of an enjoinee in the <s>Viśvajit</s> and similar cases would not arise. And when an enjoinee must be postulated there, whether the fruit-word is postulated by extension (<s>anuṣaṅga</s>) or whether a qualified person is postulated by the <s>Viśvajit</s> principle — the expectancy of the 'what-is-to-be-done' aspect (<s>itikartavyatā</s>) of the qualification-related unprecedented merit is not fulfilled. For the means-end relationship (<s>upāyopeyabhāva</s>) is understood only when there is a qualified person with respect to the supreme unprecedented merit (<s>paramāpūrva</s>). For the qualification-dependent qualification cannot be established otherwise. He whose goal is the supreme unprecedented merit is the one qualified with respect to it. Thus, just as in 'One desiring heaven should sacrifice with the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>' and the like, the means-end relationship between heaven and the sacrifice exists for the qualified person who is specified by the heaven that is to be achieved — so too here regarding firewood and the like and the supreme unprecedented merit. There, by the principle 'an effect is not for another's purpose,' the subsidiary status of firewood and the like with respect to the qualification-injunction is determined. This is called 'the grasping of the grasper' (<s>grāhakagrahaṇa</s>). And regarding the supreme unprecedented merit, confined by the origination-prescribed <s>Āgneya</s> and other topics — since subsidiary status cannot be established through any other means — the connection is only through the 'what-is-to-be-done' aspect. Refutation of this: The <s>Prābhākara</s>s [say:] This is untenable. For if the connected denotation (<s>anvitābhidhāna</s>) of every injunction along with an enjoinee is relied upon, then even the injunctions of production regarding the specific sacrifices of the <s>Rājasūya</s> would have to be accompanied by qualification. Then, for <s>Videvana</s> and others recited within the framework of the <s>Abhiṣecanīya</s>, their subsidiary status would be to the <s>Abhiṣecanīya</s>'s intermediate unprecedented merit through its topic alone. If one says: 'An injunction with unseen purpose is not expressed along with an enjoinee, but only for obtaining performance' — [then:] the <s>Abhiṣecanīya</s> and others obtain performance through the agency of the supreme unprecedented merit itself, since the supreme unprecedented merit also has them as its objects; therefore, when sacrifices that are its objects are being performed for its own accomplishment, the injunctions of production regarding them too, having obtained accomplishment, do not expect another enjoinee for their own accomplishment. Then the <s>prayāja</s> injunctions too, having assigned objects, should not require another qualification. One might think: 'Their assignment itself is impossible without qualification-dependent qualification.' That is wrong — since the connection with qualification is first understood by the word alone through mere subsidiary status of the injunction, and by the topic, assignment is through the 'what-is-to-be-done' aspect. For in the proximity of the qualification-injunction, 'He sacrifices with firewood' and the like are stated without any qualification. That qualification-injunction, being the purpose, lacking qualification itself, is expressed by its own words as connected with firewood and the like, which are themselves without purpose. And the sentences about firewood and the like present only the forms of sacrifices specified by substance and deity; through proximity alone, the connection with the qualification-injunction occurs. If proximity were not respected, then why would the person qualified with respect to the supreme unprecedented merit be postulated even for firewood and the like? Thus, the subsidiary status with respect to qualification, established through proximity alone — how does it become [the basis for an objection]? And the expectancy of 'how' arises regarding the qualification-related unprecedented merit that is to be achieved. Therefore, the door of instrumental assistance (<s>karaṇopakāra</s>) alone is relied upon for them. When the connected denotation is with subsidiary status — that is the 'grasping of the grasper.' And the postulation that their [role] is through the door of instrumental assistance — that itself is the assignment by topic. Doubt and resolution regarding the denial of intermediate unprecedented merits (<s>avāntarāpūrva</s>): 'But thus, have intermediate unprecedented merits been denied?' We shall not deny them. Although initially the injunctive suffixes cannot convey a separate injunction — since in cases like 'they thresh rice' and the like, they are suspected of merely restating a known qualification-injunction — nevertheless, since for these momentary [actions], not generating intermediate unprecedented merits, subsidiary status cannot be established, later, for the purpose of establishing subsidiary status with respect to the qualification-related unprecedented merit, the intermediate unprecedented merits, to be denoted by the injunctive suffixes, are accepted through reasoning. This has been elucidated in the <s>Dīkṣaṇīyā-vāṅniyamādhikaraṇa</s> [<s>Mīmāṃsā Sūtra</s> 9.1.2]. And we shall state in this very [section] how the acceptance of intermediate unprecedented merits operates. And the intermediate unprecedented merits are brought by words as subsidiaries toward the qualification-related unprecedented merit. Doubt and resolution regarding intermediate unprecedented merits in <s>Dīkṣaṇīya</s> and the like: 'But then, in <s>Dīkṣaṇīya</s> and the like, the speech-restriction (<s>vāṅniyama</s>) would not be caused by the intermediate unprecedented merit; rather, it would be caused by that unprecedented merit itself, like "one threshes with consecrated mortar and pestle."' No — because it is for the accomplishment of its own form. Even though the intermediate unprecedented merits are subsidiary to the supreme unprecedented merit, nevertheless, properties like speech-restriction are only for the accomplishment of their own form within them, since the relation of the intermediate unprecedented merit connected with the <s>Dīkṣaṇīya</s> with its own form is understood from 'One should recite at the <s>Dīkṣaṇīya</s>' [<s>Āpastamba Śrauta Sūtra</s> 20.4.10]. The subsidiary-principal relationship (<s>aṅgāṅgibhāva</s>) characterized by abandoning one's own form is not proper for them, since it is itself a secondary indication. Nor is there non-performance due to being for one's own form, since one's own form is established as knowable through no other means. Everything unprecedented (<s>apūrva</s>) is established solely through words; but for threshing and the like, whose accomplishment is knowable through other means of knowledge, their own form is established even without sprinkling (<s>prokṣaṇa</s>). When [their purpose is] for one's own form, the non-performance of the restriction-injunction is proper. Thus, regarding <s>prayāja</s>s and the like that have obtained performance through being subsidiaries themselves, there is no room for the postulation of qualification. By that same method, the intermediate operation of the instrument should be understood in the injunctions of production regarding the principal [sacrifices]. For one who does not accept that intermediate operation, there would be no distinction of instruments in the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s> and the like; likewise, the properties of the <s>Āgneya</s> and the like would apply to the <s>Upāṃśuyāja</s> and the like, since they equally serve the supreme unprecedented merit. But with the distinction of intermediate operations, the arrangement is proper — the instrumentality of the <s>Āgneya</s> is of one kind, and that of the <s>Upāṃśuyāja</s> is of another. Just as the arrangement of the properties of <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s> as means of praise differs — so too with the <s>Pārvaṇa</s> oblations. For this very reason, supersession (<s>bādha</s>) operates in derivative rites (<s>vikṛti</s>); for the instrumentality of the <s>Saurya</s> [sacrifice] toward the unprecedented merit is not like that of the <s>Āgneya</s>, and without the path through the model rite, the <s>Pārvaṇa</s> oblations are superseded. Those who do not call the intermediate unprecedented merits 'means' (<s>sādhanarūpa</s>) — for them there is no intermediate operation, and all the defects stated earlier follow. For intermediate operation consists in being the cause of the production of an effect; otherwise, even exertion arising from agriculture, like plowing, would be an intermediate operation in obtaining grain. Objection: 'But thus, if [subsidiary rites] are without qualification, there would be no extension (<s>atideśa</s>) to the <s>Dīkṣaṇīya</s> and the like.' We reply: Even for those without qualification, since there is no difference in their being effects (<s>kārya</s>), and since the means have not yet been produced, the expectancy of 'how' is indeed proper. Raising the <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> view regarding intermediate topics: 'But thus the intermediate topic (<s>avāntaraprakaraṇa</s>) has been accepted!' For 'the expectancy of "how" regarding what is to be done is the topic' — this is well-known among <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s>s. Refutation of intermediate topics: There is no means of valid knowledge called 'intermediate topic,' since in the absence of an object to be known, a means of knowledge is not possible. Until those intermediate unprecedented merits are cognized, all remote auxiliaries — the entire class of word-meanings — are included without distinction under the principal injunction. Afterwards, since all [auxiliaries] equally enter the qualification, there is no mutual purpose-subservience among them — so there is no possibility of being assignable by an intermediate topic. Those [auxiliaries] for which intermediate unprecedented merits are established through sentences and such — for them the merits are established there and will not transfer to the supreme unprecedented merit. Objection: 'But thus, regarding the <s>prayāja</s>s and the like, there would be the unwanted consequence of the extension of <s>Soma</s>-sacrifice properties.' This is no fault. If even for those without qualification, there were a natural expectancy of 'what-is-to-be-done' just like for those with qualification, then indeed this would follow. But since they are not to be independently performed, there is no natural expectancy of 'what-is-to-be-done.' 'But how can there be duty-status (<s>kāryatā</s>) and yet non-performability?' — Surely you have not heard the Seventh Topic and the like! For the Guru has clearly stated there: That which a person understands independently as 'this is my duty' — that is to be performed (<s>anuṣṭheya</s>). But that which, for the accomplishment of that [duty], being previously unestablished, is good and is assigned — that is an effect (<s>kārya</s>). The supreme unprecedented merit is understood independently as a duty. For the understanding of fruit [follows] from the understanding of duty, not duty from the understanding of fruit — this was thoroughly discussed in the Sixth Topic and the like. Therefore, the distinction between what is to be performed and what is a duty is established. Establishing unprecedented merit in <s>prayāja</s>s and the like: The expectancy of 'how' arises only regarding what is to be performed, not regarding mere duty. 'Then, just as in <s>prayāja</s>s, the extension should be denied by denying the expectancy even in <s>Dīkṣaṇīya</s> and the like.' Our view has not been properly understood. For our established conclusion is this: there is no natural expectancy of 'what-is-to-be-done' for those without qualification; but an expectancy arising from another cause is not denied. Regarding the <s>Dīkṣaṇīya</s> and the like, the expectancy of 'what-is-to-be-done' is postulated through the observation of <s>prayāja</s>s and the like. For even one that is naturally without expectancy may properly have expectancy based on the incidence of another cause. Just as for the pair of words '<s>paṭo bhavati</s>' ('there is a cloth'), which are without expectancy, upon the utterance of the word <s>rakta</s> ('red'), an expectancy for 'red' [arises]. Otherwise, there would be the unwanted consequence of non-connection in '<s>raktaḥ paṭo bhavati</s>' ('the cloth is red'). Thus, in <s>prayāja</s>s, since there is no cause for raising an expectancy, there is no extension of <s>Soma</s>-sacrifice properties; and it is established that in <s>Dīkṣaṇīya</s> and the like, the characteristics of <s>Iṣṭi</s>-rites are obtained. But for those who, by accepting qualification-dependent qualification, declare subsidiary injunctions to be accompanied by qualification — for them, in <s>prayāja</s>s, by the principle of nocturnal sessions (<s>rātrisatra</s>), only the one desiring the fruit declared in the <s>arthavāda</s> would be the qualified person — so qualification-dependent qualification is not possible. One might think: 'The expectancy of "what-is-to-be-done" of the principal injunction is not fulfilled.' Let it not be fulfilled — the purpose, however, is fulfilled, since <s>arthavāda</s> words are instruments that enter the evidential portion; so that their operation may not be remote, the qualified person who desires the fruit taught by them is proper. But through the mere proximity of a qualified injunction, those without qualification that are understood as subsidiary to it do not have an expectancy of qualification — therefore, the <s>arthavāda</s> words terminate in being <s>arthavāda</s> alone. Likewise, in passages such as 'Milk is the vow of the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>' [<s>Taittirīya Āraṇyaka</s> 2.8; <s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 6.2.5.2] and the like, just as for one who has commenced eating, the restriction on the acquisition of substances [operates] — since the qualified person is obtained in one's own sentence, qualification cannot be postulated for one who has commenced the principal [rite]; otherwise, the independence of the milk-vow and the like would follow. Likewise, in 'One should not speak untruth' [<s>Taittirīya Saṃhitā</s> 2.5.5.6], even though studied in the topic, since the qualification of the agent of the prohibited action is understood, there is no possibility of entering the topic. Likewise, in 'He makes an oblation when [the vessel] is broken' — since the occasion (<s>nimitta</s>) qualifies the qualified person, without postulating the occasion, the specific qualified person is not obtained, and therefore the oblation does not obtain subsidiary status to the <s>Darśapūrṇamāsa</s>. 'We do not accept this solution here.' Since the word <s>bhinna</s> ('broken') is derived, when it applies to the topic at hand, even for a qualified person with an occasion, the qualification of the qualified person [operates] — since 'broken' is not assigned in the topic. For what is present in a topic is that which is assigned there; 'broken' is not assigned. Moreover, when an expectancy of qualification arises and one begins to postulate qualification — why is qualification postulated through the meaning and proximity? Let there be extension (<s>anuṣaṅga</s>) of the directly heard qualification-word. But when the qualification-word is heard in the principal sentence, and the connection with the principal obtains, for the proximate [subsidiaries] that have no heard qualification — since there is no expectancy of qualification when they are connected through qualified subsidiary status — the fundamental reasoning for refuting extension [applies]. But the mere accumulation (<s>abhyuccaya</s>) is better than extension, since the fulfillment of the expectancy of 'what-is-to-be-done' [operates]. Doubt and resolution regarding optionality of <s>prayāja</s>s and the like: Moreover, since in each case — 'He sacrifices with firewood' and the like — the qualification of the one qualified by the principal is understood individually, and since the subsidiary-to-principal relationship of firewood and the like operates individually, there would be individual 'what-is-to-be-done' status. For then the intermediate injunctions postulate the means-status of their own objects; since in the supreme unprecedented merit confined to the instrument, instrumentality is not possible — the postulation of means-status is only through generating instrumental assistance. Then, since the means-status is obtained independently without mutual dependence, and since each generates one instrumental assistance individually, there would be optionality (<s>vikalpa</s>) among firewood and the like. But through the qualification-injunction, when only their subsidiary status is grasped — since the connection of that [injunction] with them cannot be otherwise established — the capacity to generate instrumental assistance must be postulated for establishing subsidiary status, and that [capacity] operates according to the connection. And in the connection, all of them [operate] simultaneously. If there were individual capacity to generate instrumental assistance, then, given optionality, the connection would not be extended as in obligatory [rites]. But when the capacity of the aggregate to generate it is relied upon, the extension of connection in every case [follows] — so there is no individual 'what-is-to-be-done' status. In the means-end relationship, given connection through subsidiary status, since the means-status is optional, the connection too is accordingly — and that is proper. The connected denotation (<s>anvitābhidhāna</s>) of the injunctive suffixes conveys their own meaning as connected with the unprecedented merit through subsidiary status, and the topic arranges the door of instrumental assistance. And through the instrumental operation of adoption characterized by the injunctive function, the subsidiary status of the auxiliaries in aggregate — the generating of instrumental assistance — is postulated for each topic, and the arrangement of subsidiaries [is determined] topic by topic. Determination of the object of measurement (<s>kāryaprameya</s>): Where and for which [rites] is the subsidiary status based on duty? For model-rite [components] with respect to derivative unprecedented merits and their instruments — what they call extension (<s>atideśa</s>); and for model-rite [components] falling in the place of model-rite [substances] with respect to something else — what they call adaptation (<s>ūha</s>). Both are twofold: verbal/taught (<s>aupadeśika</s>) and duty-born (<s>kāryaja</s>). There, regarding the derivative unprecedented merit that is to be achieved, having the expectancy of 'what-is-to-be-done' with the instrument, when the instrument is obtained in the meaning of the productive force (<s>bhāvārtha</s>) — the further expectancy of 'what-is-to-be-done' [arises], and for that, the postulation of an alternative assistance as in the model rite does not work. For if an alternative assistance were established, the subsequent expectancy for the two types of word-meanings generating it would not be fulfilled by the connection with the class of word-meanings studied in the topic. But when the model-rite assistance is accepted, through it the presentation of the two types of model-rite word-meanings fulfills the expectancy — thus, it accepts only the model-rite assistance. Determination that inference and analogy (<s>anumāna</s> and <s>upamāna</s>) as accepted by the <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> school are not causes of extension: What, then, is the cause for acceptance? Not inference, due to the absence of an invariable logical mark (<s>liṅga</s>)-relation. Not analogy, since it pertains only to similarity, and since these two, grasping established objects, have no validity regarding duties (<s>kārya</s>). The denotation of model-rite assistance by the injunctive suffixes: We reply: That very injunctive word (<s>liṅ</s> and the like) which denotes the injunction — it itself denotes its own meaning as connected with the model-rite assistance. Even in the model rite, the injunctive [suffix] itself speaks its own meaning as connected with the assistance postulated for the injunctive purpose. And in connected denotation, expectancy (<s>ākāṅkṣā</s>), fitness (<s>yogyatā</s>), and proximity (<s>sannidhi</s>) are the causes. Here, the expectancy and fitness of the model-rite assistance alone are undisputed. Proximity, however: through the model-rite unprecedented merit itself, known in the mind, and through the injunctive qualifier, the model-rite unprecedented merit becomes present in the mind, and it presents its own assistance. Therefore the connection of assistance is called 'taught' (<s>aupadeśika</s>) by the knowers of truth. Presentation of the taught nature of assistance in derivative rites: That which is presented by a text or by the purpose of an injunction and enters into connection — that is 'taught.' For example: assistance in the model rite; or the qualified person in <s>Viśvajit</s> and the like. Thus, when the assistance has obtained its connection, the expectancy regarding which class of word-meanings generates it arises subsequently for the derivative unprecedented merit. Objection: 'But in the model rite, this assistance already has a known class of word-meanings as its generators — so there is no cause for the arising of expectancy. For this very reason, they think there is no extension of word-meanings.' If there were a subsequent expectancy even regarding word-meanings, then, given the connection of the model-rite [components] with the derivative unprecedented merit through that cause — who would prevent the extension of word-meanings just like the extension of assistance? For the knowers of extension say: 'The connection of what belongs to one with another is extension.' Refutation: Here we say — if the model-rite word-meanings were caused by instrumental assistance, then when the generators are known, the expectancy regarding the principal would not arise. But the properties are caused by the unprecedented merit, say the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s>s. This being so, since those properties that are caused by the unprecedented merit have their generative capacity postulated only in the assistance connected with it, not in assistance connected with something else — therefore, the expectancy of means that have not been produced regarding the connection with the derivative unprecedented merit is not untenable. But for those word-meanings whose means-status is already established, there is only performance — since their [connection] is taught, there should be neither adaptation (<s>ūha</s>) nor supersession (<s>bādha</s>) of the assistance-means relationship. But when the connection with the derivative unprecedented merit is based on expectancy — we shall state here how adaptation and supersession are accomplished. And thus, when there is the expectancy of word-meanings, those model-rite word-meanings that come within the scope of the mind through the assistance subsequently enter into connection. Presentation of how assistance presents model-rite word-meanings: 'By what connection does the assistance present them?' We reply: In the model rite, between those word-meanings and that assistance, the relation of cause and effect is cognized; through that prior cognition, memory regarding them arises. When those [word-meanings], brought into proximity by memory, have obtained connection — subsequently, the means-status for generating assistance is postulated for their aggregate, according to the topic in which they are studied. As they say: 'The derivative class of word-meanings, together with the model-rite assistance brought to bear, and the injunction postulating the means as unified in the assistance — the knowledge of the connection of the model-rite word-meanings presented by the effect characterized as assistance, which is duty-born with respect to the derivative unprecedented merit — that is called verbal (<s>śābda</s>). Nor is the connection of word-meanings with another unprecedented merit impossible; for there is no [rule] preventing the connection of what belongs to one with another.' [<s>Bṛhatī Ṭīkā</s> 10.1.1.] And the meaning of this is thoroughly discussed in the <s>Ṛjuvimalā</s> and other works. Determination of the verbal nature of adaptation (<s>ūha</s>): Regarding the model-rite purificatory rites (<s>saṃskāra</s>) and the determination of the connection of word-meanings falling in the place of the model-rite substance — adaptation (<s>ūha</s>), by another name, is also duty-born verbal [cognition]. When the effect cognized in the model rite regarding threshing and the like is determined as 'this is that very one' — the determination of their connection with a different derivative substance [follows]. For threshing and the like, whose purpose is the unprecedented merit — the model-rite substance to be purified by threshing and the like, such as paddy-grain, is the scriptural meaning in the model rite. In the derivative rite too, <s>nīvāra</s> and other [grains] are of the same kind — hence, adaptation of their properties to them. Determination of supersession (<s>bādha</s>): Thus, when threshing and the like have been adapted with respect to <s>kṛṣṇala</s> and other [substances], the determination of supersession through the absence of the intermediate effect — that too is duty-born. Thus it is established that the model-rite assistance in the derivative rite is generated by word-meanings that have been adapted, superseded, and accumulated. Determination of economy (<s>tantra</s>) and repetition (<s>āvāpa</s>): For those auxiliaries that are 'taught' and those that are connected with the duty — when there is connection with multiple principals — the specialization of performance is economy (<s>tantra</s>). Likewise, the difference of place, time, and agent — which are concomitants of performance — is not determined when the duty itself is not different. But when the duty differs, performance for the sake of the duty repeats itself. Even when place and the like differ, since the difference of performance is understood, there is indeed repetition of performance.

children.text: iti mahāmahopādhyāyaśrīmacchālikanāthamiśrapraṇītāyāṃ prakaraṇapañcikāyāmaṅgapārāyaṇe ārādupakārakāṅganirūpaṇaparo nāma dvitīyaḥ paricchedassamāptaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Prakaraṇapañcikā</s> composed by the illustrious <s>Mahāmahopādhyāya Śrīmac-Śālikanātha Miśra</s>, the second section (<s>pariccheda</s>) named the Traversal of Ancillary Elements (<s>Aṅgapārāyaṇa</s>), devoted to the determination of remotely beneficial ancillaries, is concluded.
Now begins the fourteenth chapter (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) named the Traversal of Extended Application (<s>Atideśapārāyaṇa</s>).
Declaration of the chapter's subject:
Those who do not accept the extended application (<s>atideśa</s>) of ritual elements (<s>padārtha</s>) to the modified rite (<s>vikṛti</s>),
and [who deny] the instruction of the procedure (<s>prakāra</s>) — the reply to them is now stated.
Presentation of our own doctrine:
Through the primary beneficial [element] (<s>prākṛta upakāra</s>) and the modified ritual elements (<s>vaikṛta padārtha</s>),
the injunction (<s>vidhi</s>), connected through its own procedural rule, is said to be syntactically connected (<s>anvita</s>).
Whatever is desired, fit, and proximate —
the meaning of the injunction, connected with that, is expressed by its own words.
And the meaning of the injunction, being what is to be accomplished (<s>sādhya</s>), requires beneficial support (<s>upakāra</s>);
the primary [support], being fit, is made proximate through sentences etc.
Since [the primary support] cannot be known otherwise, even though preceded by ancillary elements,
that primary beneficial [element] is made proximate in the modified rite (<s>vikṛti</s>).
Nevertheless, the injunction first accepts the procedure (<s>prakāra</s>) because it is required,
but disregards the ritual elements even though they are already known.
Afterwards, however, with those [ritual elements] too, for the establishment of beneficial support,
being required, and obtained through the force of that [procedure], it achieves syntactic connection.
The syntactic connection everywhere is considered to be through the relation of subordinate and principal (<s>guṇa-pradhāna</s>);
the principal is the injunction (<s>vidhi</s>), i.e. <s>dharma</s>, and the subordinate elements are accepted as [serving] that.
And the expression of what is connected is not beyond what is presented by words —
as seen in the <s>Pitṛyajña</s> etc., even with a hypothetically constructed (<s>kalpya</s>) eligible person.
Not everything related achieves syntactic expression all at once,
but rather in sequence according to the order of proximity of the related [elements].
Specific presentation of the primary (<s>prakṛti</s>) and modified (<s>vikṛti</s>) [rites]:
In the primary rite, however, because the ritual elements have their own words, their connection comes first;
the connection of the hypothetically constructed beneficial [element] comes afterwards — this alone is the difference.
Definition of extended application (<s>atideśa</s>): Through beneficial [elements] in reversed order and through the modified ritual elements,
the injunction becomes connected with the primary [elements] — that is accepted as extended application (<s>atideśa</s>).
The application of an injunction belonging to one context to another context as well —
extended application is appropriate for both procedure (<s>prakāra</s>) and <s>dharma</s> properties.
Just as the procedure belonging to one context achieves connection in another,
so too the <s>dharma</s> properties are accepted [to be transferable] — their transferability is acknowledged.
Doubt regarding conflict with the tenth [section] etc., according to a partial view:
But this position of yours entails a conflict with the tenth [section] etc.!
Not so — this extended application, being independent of the obligatory effect, has been excluded [from that conflict].
If the connection of <s>dharma</s> properties were through the relation of 'being-like-that' (<s>tadvadbhāva</s>),
then, since the procedure would not be relied upon, understanding would not be established.
Refutation of that:
Just as in the primary rite, when the connection of the ritual elements is known,
a door — whether seen or unseen — is constructed for the purpose of connection.
Similarly, when the connection independent of the obligatory effect is known,
a door — whether seen or unseen — would have to be constructed in the modified rite too.
Therefore, the sublation based on the loss of the obligatory effect does not work,
since even in the absence of a seen [door], an unseen door is possible.

children.text: kāryāpekṣā yadā dharmā vikṛtau yānti saṅgatim /
children.translated_text: When the <s>dharma</s> properties, dependent on the obligatory effect, achieve connection in the modified rite,
then through the loss of the obligatory effect, their sublation is established.
For the <s>dharma</s> properties, endowed with a door, obtain [connection] through the obligatory effect;
'they obtain' — hence there is no occasion for constructing a [separate] door then.

children.text:
kāryānapekṣasambandho dharmāṇāmucyate yadi /
daśamādyavirodhassyāttadānīṃ na ca tattathā // 23 // 11//
children.translated_text:
If it is said that the connection of <s>dharma</s> properties is independent of the obligatory effect,
then a conflict with the tenth [section] etc. would arise — but that is not so.

children.text: tadvadbhāvena kiṃ dharmāḥ prakāro vāpi gṛhyate /
children.translated_text: Is it the <s>dharma</s> properties or the procedure that is grasped through 'being-like-that'?
This reflection in the tenth [section] etc. is for establishing sublation.
Presentation of the conflict with the tenth [section] etc. according to our view:
The opponent there says: the acceptance of ritual elements [is primary];

children.text: nopakāre hi dharmebhyo vinā śakyaṃ rirūpaṇam // 25 //
children.translated_text: for without <s>dharma</s> properties, beneficial support cannot be determined.
Although the injunction itself first requires the procedure,
nevertheless, even in the primary rite, [the procedure's] own essential nature
is not fully known, but rather through the <s>dharma</s> properties as heard;
therefore, the determination [of procedure] always follows the ritual elements.
Hence, since the ritual elements are known first, the modified
injunction achieves connection through the ritual elements; having grasped them, it then itself
does not warrant sublation of the primary beneficial support when the door is not lost.
Description of the established conclusion of the tenth [section] etc. according to our view:
The proponent of the established conclusion says thus: True, the <s>dharma</s> properties come first;
even so,
even though they are not grasped, at that time they are not required.
For the injunction, being of the nature of what is to be accomplished, requires the procedure again;
not the ritual elements — for it disregards them even though already known.
It first achieves connection with the procedure alone;
afterwards with the ritual elements constructed through the procedure — this has been shown.
Doubt and its resolution regarding whether properties of one [rite] can belong to another:
How can <s>dharma</s> properties belonging to one [rite] achieve connection in another?
If so, the same [objection] applies to beneficial support too — hence it is said:
'The beneficial support has no connection' — this is a laughable statement;
for if that [support] did not belong to another [rite], how then would it be transferred?
For the transfer of what belongs to one context to another is specifically called extended application (<s>atideśa</s>);
in its obtaining through 'being-like-that,' there is no contradiction.
For the purpose of establishing 'being-like-that,' the same [reasoning] applies to ritual elements too;
this contradiction of 'what-belongs-to-one not connecting with another'

children.text: mukhāntareṇa15 sambandhe sa ca nāsti kathañcana /
children.translated_text: does not exist in any way when the connection is through another channel.
Presentation of the impossibility according to the <s>Bhāṭṭa</s> view:

children.text: ye tu necchanti dharmāṇāṃ sambandhaṃ vaikṛtaissaha // 37 //
children.translated_text: But those who do not accept the connection of <s>dharma</s> properties with the modified [rite] —
the text of the primary ancillary elements in the <s>apūrva</s> [section] is contradicted for them.
Their reflection on the obtaining of procedure in the seventh and eighth [sections]

children.text: na yuktaṃ tatra cintā hi ṣaṭke 'sminkāryabandhanā /
children.translated_text: is not justified, for in this group of six, reflection is bound to the obligatory effect;
if compulsion (<s>niyoga</s>) too is an obligatory effect, then reflection for that purpose too [is required].

The reflection of the fourth chapter too would fall within this group of six in the same way.

Demonstration of the establishment according to our view:
For from the obligatory effect, the meaning of the instruction and the meaning of the injunction etc. are understood.
Just as its having been instructed, so too its implication —
will be stated.
Therefore, setting aside the meaning of the injunction, another obligatory [element] is resorted to.
This reflection, serving as a door, is enjoined in the group of six regarding obligatory effects;
therefore, the extended application of ritual elements is considered within this group of six.
The beneficial support too of that very [element] serving as a cause has been shown;
in [the passage] 'he consecrates with six [verses],' of the primary [elements] with the modified ones —
the sublation of the non-ancillary by the ancillary [elements] thus follows,
for the establishment of beneficial support, since [the non-ancillary] is external to the status of principal.

children.text:
naiva prayuktimātreṇa kriyate prākṛtaṃ punaḥ /
tatra /
kāryātideśoyaṃ sammatastvaupadeśikaḥ // 45 // 18//
children.translated_text:
The primary [element] is not [transferred] merely by being employed.
Regarding that:
This extended application of the obligatory effect is accepted as instructional (<s>aupadeśika</s>).
It is constructed through the meaning of the injunction, which is the object of instruction;
the construction of beneficial support in the primary rite through the <s>apūrva</s> [unseen merit]
and [the construction] of the one to be enjoined (<s>niyojya</s>) are accepted through the instruction of the elders.
Presentation of the meaning of the word 'instruction' (<s>upadeśa</s>) according to our view:
For instruction (<s>upadeśa</s>)
is called merely the textual composition here.
And that [instruction] has been determined to be a valid means of knowledge regarding the meaning of the injunction in the form of the obligatory;
the meaning that is understood from which [source] — that alone, and nothing beyond, is instructional (<s>aupadeśika</s>).
The meaning of the injunction, through its own cognition, whatever it implies — that too,
while not culminating in the meaning of the injunction, whatever it is capable of constructing —
instructional status is appropriate for that too, just as for what is known through the syllables;
but the injunction is not capable of constructing a specific beneficial support,
nor a specific ritual element — the modified as the primary does;
although capable of constructing a specific beneficial support,
it grasps [the support] from the primary rite itself — economy (<s>lāghava</s>) is the reason there;
for in the conflict between what is already established and what needs to be constructed, acceptance of the established is more economical.
And that established [support] is made proximate through sentences, names, and grammatical gender that are not its own,
but the obtaining of different ritual elements would not be possible without beneficial support.
Statement of the specifics of primary and modified [rites]:
The obtaining of those [elements] is from the obligatory effect, and the procedure from instruction;
in the primary rite, both the beneficial support and the ritual element are from instruction.
In the modified rite, the <s>dharma</s> properties are from the obligatory effect, and the procedure from instruction.
Presentation of our view:
Even when this is instructed, the expression by the word <s>atideśa</s> (extended application)
is not precluded — its meaning is the otherness of context from one's own injunction.
Exposing the fault in the <s>Bhāṭṭa</s> view which claims that instruction and extended application have different domains:
Being instructed and being transferred are not contradictory for one and the same [element];
for instruction and extended application are not [two separate] valid means of knowledge [in our view].
If instruction and extended application are [two separate] valid means for you,
Description of the absence of the previously stated fault according to our view:

children.text: tadā virodho jāyeta na caivamiha sammatam // 58 //
children.translated_text: then contradiction would arise — but it is not so accepted here.
Therefore, because it is the object of instruction, it is accepted as instructed;
and since it exists in another [context] from another [source], extended application is also appropriate.
Specification of the domains of instruction and extended application according to our view:
Both the group of six regarding instruction and regarding obligatory-effect-as-valid-means —
neither depends on instruction alone, nor on extended application alone.

children.text: atideśāśrayatve hi bādhe tantre ca bhūyasī /
children.translated_text: For if [the group of six] depended on extended application, in cases of sublation and archetype,
the extensive reflection regarding the subject of the instructed meaning would simply not be tenable.
But when depending on the door-obligatory-effect, the tenability of all
reflections [is established] — therefore, reflection here is properly dependent on the obligatory effect.
Doubt whether ritual elements too have instructional status like beneficial support:
But then the instructional status of ritual elements too would follow,
since through their obligatory nature too, the meaning of the injunction is said to be connected.
Refutation of that:
We reply: thus there would be verbal [cognition], not being-the-object-of-instruction;
this distinction between the two valid means is based on the mode of presentation.
That which, presented through instruction, achieves syntactic connection with the sentence-meaning —
that is to be known as instructional (<s>aupadeśika</s>); and it is presented in two ways:
Presented through the text itself, and presented through the meaning of the injunction —
just as the beneficial support in the primary rite, and the one to be enjoined (<s>niyojya</s>), as heard.
But that which is presented through the procedure is not presented in two ways;
therefore, it is not instructional — it is merely bound to the obligatory effect.
By <s>Śālikanātha</s>, who strives to remove the delusion of the previously established doctrines,
this effort has been made, bringing delight to the accomplished.

children.text: iti mahāmahopādhyāyaśrīmacchālikanāthamiśrapraṇītāyāṃ prakaraṇapañcikāyāmatideśapārāyaṇaṃ nāma caturdaśaṃ prakaraṇaṃ samāptam //
children.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Prakaraṇapañcikā</s> composed by the illustrious <s>Mahāmahopādhyāya Śrīmac-Śālikanātha Miśra</s>, the fourteenth chapter named the Traversal of Extended Application (<s>Atideśapārāyaṇa</s>) is concluded.
And thus is concluded this <s>Prakaraṇapañcikā</s>.
